legacyText.1135040182: He is wearing a cardigan with one elbow held together by safety pins. His hair is flattened on one side as if he has been asleep against a book.
legacyText.2287218125: “You nearly sent your return line through an open channel,” he says. Then he notices Miso. “Oh, good. It's your fault.”
legacyText.2564163754: “Don't Julian me. I've been here since Wednesday.”
legacyText.2052435586: He lets me in. Beyond the door lies a room full of empty telephone booths. Their glass panels reflect a sky full of stars, although there are no windows.
legacyText.963885348: One booth at the back is lit. In it, a telephone rings beneath a handwritten sign.
legacyText.3882134374: DO NOT PICK UP TO SEE WHO IT IS.
legacyText.116184402: Underneath, someone has added: YES, THIS MEANS YOU, JULIAN.
legacyText.3445844565: Julian puts the kettle on, checks the water level, and takes it off again.
legacyText.2930700426: “Never mind. It might be river water.”
legacyText.188874457: I follow his gaze to a stain on the ceiling. It has the shape of the building above me, though the building changes while I watch. A chimney disappears. A fire escape grows down through one edge. My own kitchen window opens briefly in the middle.
legacyText.3990569806: “Is that how you saw the flat?” I ask Miso.
legacyText.573449099: He jumps onto a desk and settles his tail over his paws. “One way.”
legacyText.4127159941: Julian makes a sound that suggests there are several worse ways.
legacyText.83731572: He is nineteen, he tells me, studying part-time and working for the small independent archive attached to the annex. He says independent with a care that suggests he has already had to explain it to a tax office. Most of the collection is ordinary: old operator manuals, repair logs, donated equipment. The part that isn't ordinary has been making his working week increasingly difficult.
legacyText.1168067928: “My supervisor used to deal with that bit.”
legacyText.3508910675: For that sentence alone, I could forgive him a lot. He seems to realise he has offered something larger than he meant to, because he begins moving papers into neat piles.
legacyText.2252472511: Imani points to it. “What happens if somebody picks up?”
legacyText.1661265448: “Usually someone asks for somebody who isn't there. If you tell them they're wrong, they try the next place. If you offer to help, the system decides you're available.”
legacyText.2591236880: The cat answers. “To carry the message.”
legacyText.1195216845: He says it as if that should explain everything. I wait until he notices I haven't understood.
legacyText.2710549205: “The original line let a caller send a message without making the receiver answer. Whoever built this version removed that safeguard.”
legacyText.3225177132: Julian takes a recorder from a drawer. It is the same model as the one in the annex. A strip of tape on its back says NADIA: BACKUP.
legacyText.3713150228: My mother speaks when he presses play.
legacyText.1567815443: “Test forty-three. The holding mark remains temporary. Seven minutes if the line is stable. Less if it isn't. We need a second reader at the receiving end. Adrian says we can automate the acknowledgement. I disagree.”
legacyText.2935968079: A pause. A paper being turned. In the background I hear myself, younger, complaining about homework. Julian stops the recorder when he sees my face.
legacyText.4294429762: Mum's voice returns. She describes a circuit she has been testing, then corrects herself, then starts the explanation again without recording over the first attempt. I have spent months trying to preserve every memory I have of her. Here she is getting annoyed at a loose battery cover.
legacyText.3535045211: I need to sit down. I do it before anybody asks.
legacyText.2571416637: The recording ends with her saying, “{{firstName}}, don't put that near the—” and a loud clatter.
legacyText.4071194512: I remember the day. I dropped a screwdriver into a ceramic mug she'd been using to hold broken components. I thought she was angry because it was her favourite mug. Now, listening to the quick movement afterwards, I wonder what else was inside it.
legacyText.3998961228: Julian slides the recorder across the desk.
legacyText.3666156762: “Why haven't you given this to Leila?”
legacyText.2438942714: “Because I couldn't get back through the door until someone dialled the full return address. I did tell you about Wednesday.”
legacyText.27612164: I take the chalk from its box. On the desk I draw the holding mark, exactly as I drew it in the cupboard. Julian sets an old desk fan beside it and plugs the fan into a socket. Nothing happens.
legacyText.736639731: “Magic doesn't work because chalk is expensive,” he says. “That shape holds a relationship. You need to tell it what relationship.”
legacyText.314013591: I point to the notebook. “It doesn't say that.”
legacyText.1508358263: “It does. In the little note you skipped.”
legacyText.3099040130: It does. I skipped the note because it looked like a caption.
legacyText.665878981: He puts my hand on the fan's plug, then makes me describe the connection between the socket and the motor. I say electricity. He asks what electricity is doing. I say making the fan spin. He asks what I want to stop.
legacyText.2444871254: “Then you want the mechanism, not the connection.”
legacyText.3439655513: Imani, who has been crouching beside the fan, turns its power switch on. It begins to rattle.
legacyText.553270804: I let go of the plug. I want to laugh, but the room has started to feel unfair. My mother did something here that kept her away for eleven months. There should be a more difficult explanation than a switch I didn't notice.
legacyText.524794084: Julian tears a sheet of paper in half and writes YOUR END on one piece, MY END on the other. He gives one to me.
legacyText.883405714: “Try it on something that needs two people.”
legacyText.425660583: I put the paper on the desk. Imani holds the second half. When I close the final line of the chalk mark, the two pieces rise an inch from the wood and stay there.
legacyText.432010129: My fingers ache. I concentrate on the torn edges, on where they would fit together. The paper begins to shake.
legacyText.2834378289: Julian starts a timer. I hold the mark for forty-one seconds before my hand cramps and the papers fall.
legacyText.3676381830: It feels like failure until he writes forty-one in the margin beside my mother's first test.
legacyText.1001351824: At the back of the room, the ringing phone stops. A printer I hadn't noticed begins feeding out paper. Julian reaches it before the sheet can fall.
legacyText.1204886521: Three lines are printed across the top.
legacyText.643448959: It is Friday morning. I have two days.
legacyText.2234577607: The collection schedule gives me a deadline and no address. I turn the paper over as if the missing information might be on the back.
legacyText.24550017: Julian takes it away before I wear a hole through it.
legacyText.4191692151: “We have to trace an earlier call. Same receiving point, older sender. There'll be an acknowledgement.”
legacyText.3756204756: He raises one eyebrow at the notebook in my hand.
legacyText.3807505472: Miso leads me to a booth with a cracked pane. Behind the glass, a telephone sits beside a sewing basket. An empty chair faces a window full of afternoon sunshine. It is bright enough to make my eyes hurt after the long night.
legacyText.3114429809: “This was Celia Bell's,” Julian says. “A volunteer operator. She died before the connection broke. Her channel's been replaying because the last message never reached its destination.”
legacyText.94082809: “Gone on. This is what she left.”
legacyText.2399375019: He doesn't offer a simpler explanation. I am beginning to appreciate that about him.
legacyText.2385126628: The door opens into a flat full of warm air and the smell of something baking. A radio plays softly in the kitchen. There are birthday cards on the mantelpiece, several months of them displayed together. On the table beside the telephone lies an envelope addressed to a man called Martin.
legacyText.2347812308: A woman in a green cardigan sits by the window. When I come in, she looks up and smiles.
legacyText.1815914853: “I rang yesterday. They said they'd send somebody.”
legacyText.3065054537: Imani stays in the doorway. Miso sniffs the woman's shoes, then moves to the telephone.
legacyText.3296532011: The woman doesn't react to him. She repeats her question.
legacyText.3694428599: I understand then, a little. The room is starting over. The radio plays the same two notes. The kitchen clock clicks back from twelve to eleven.
legacyText.3566634948: On the envelope, the ink of Martin's name runs down the paper.
legacyText.1568768267: Julian points towards a cabinet behind the woman's chair. “Routing book. We need the entries for last March.”
legacyText.641189410: I could walk around her. She isn't watching me; her gaze is fixed on the door, waiting for a person who must be taking a long time. But her hand rests on the cabinet's drawer, and when Julian tries to open it she grips the handle.
legacyText.3895043866: I look at the letter. The envelope hasn't been sealed. A faint rectangle marks the place where a stamp should be.
legacyText.4244457259: For the first time her eyes follow me. They are a cloudy blue, with the red rims of someone who hasn't slept well.
legacyText.3847170065: She gestures to the envelope. The street name has almost disappeared. I write it down before it can go entirely.
legacyText.12046108: Julian shifts his weight. “{{firstName}}. We can't start taking on every—”
legacyText.1932702564: “I said can we. I haven't said I will.”
legacyText.1997931278: Mrs. Bell looks towards the kitchen. A timer sounds once and dies.
legacyText.220742028: “I told him not to come,” she says. “He was driving in that weather. I said it could wait until Tuesday.”
legacyText.577444747: I sit on the edge of the sofa. The cushion has a dent where someone must have sat for years.
legacyText.1073949457: She looks relieved, and then unhappy, and then relieved again. The room doesn't seem able to decide which part to keep.
legacyText.897249495: Imani takes out her phone. There is no signal, but she types the address into a note.
legacyText.627743571: “We can find out whether he still lives there,” she says. “That's a thing we can actually promise.”
legacyText.3391732764: Inside, the routing book is an ordinary ledger with ruled columns. Most of the entries are numbers. In the margin beside Nadia {{surname}}, a small cross has been drawn through the return line. Under it, my mother's writing says: Received at lower station. Witness present: A. Voss. Ask why he didn't sign.
legacyText.3080236847: I photograph the page. On my screen, the photograph shows only a blank ledger.
legacyText.1895905905: “Pen,” Julian says, passing me one. “Paper holds. Cameras copy the wrong layer.”
legacyText.1774372205: I write the entry in my notebook, including the little cross and the exact position of the unsigned box.
legacyText.1896543588: The woman reaches for the letter. Her fingers go through it.
legacyText.3928733487: Miso stands beside the door, tail rigid. “We should leave.”
legacyText.1022351860: The room has begun to tilt. Cups slide across the mantelpiece. Imani catches my sleeve as the sofa shifts away from the wall. I take the envelope with my other hand and pull back towards the booth.
legacyText.489781722: Mrs. Bell has stopped looking at me. She is watching the window.
legacyText.2087376317: “Tell him it wasn't because I didn't want him,” she says.
legacyText.1450086370: I cannot tell whether she's asking me or remembering a conversation she already had.
legacyText.4127368998: Back in the exchange room, the glass pane cracks from top to bottom. The flat goes dark. My watch says six minutes and forty-eight seconds have passed.
legacyText.1900712605: Julian closes the booth door carefully.
legacyText.4125070381: “You're going to need to decide,” he says, “which promises fit in two days.”
legacyText.3195577784: I put the envelope inside the notebook, where the address won't rub away.
legacyText.1039456055: The letter has an address on a street Julian says isn't far from the exchange room's ordinary exit. It is still early enough that the shops have their shutters down. I stand under an awning while a delivery driver drags crates into a bakery and wonder whether showing up at a stranger's house before seven counts as a worse idea when the letter comes from his dead mother.
legacyText.3358322339: Imani checks the note in her phone.
legacyText.450303444: “We can leave it. We promised to find out whether he lives there. Not make him open it.”
legacyText.3861066963: Julian is carrying the evidence box against his chest. He has been looking at the time every few minutes.
legacyText.2278271211: “Your aunt thinks we're on our way back.”
legacyText.1395472227: “So tell her where we are,” Imani says.
legacyText.3753489007: I do. Leila replies with an address confirmation and a request to stay together. No lecture. It is almost more difficult to argue with.
legacyText.2068503672: The house has a small front garden full of snow-covered pots. Two bins stand by the side gate. A light is on in the kitchen. Through the glass beside the door I can see a coat rack with far more coats than the space was designed to hold.
legacyText.2244789723: A man in slippers opens the door. He looks at the three of us, then at the box, then at Miso. His hand stays on the latch.
legacyText.689506359: Fair question. I give my first name and explain that the letter was found among papers belonging to his mother. It is a careful explanation. I don't enjoy how much it resembles Leila's earlier ones.
legacyText.149187410: He takes it, examines the handwriting and leans one shoulder against the door frame. For a moment he seems too tired to keep being suspicious.
legacyText.2168012419: “In an archive,” Julian says. “She worked as a volunteer operator. We're cataloguing a group of personal papers.”
legacyText.950460264: Not entirely true. Not entirely false. Martin looks at the box again and accepts enough of it to stop asking at the door.
legacyText.1151453134: He doesn't invite me in. I am glad. It means I don't have to explain which part of my reason for being there is a trespass into his life.
legacyText.864473758: He turns the envelope over. The back is unsealed.
legacyText.2206946429: I could have. In the exchange room, during the long wait for the door. In Dennis's car. On the pavement. The notebook has been full of things I needed to know, and it would have been easy to put the letter in the same category.
legacyText.320685958: Martin nods once. He opens it while I stand on the step. His eyes move quickly over the first lines, then stop.
legacyText.1483048946: Behind him, someone in the kitchen asks whether he needs help. He says no without looking away from the page.
legacyText.3008975615: I feel I should leave. Nobody has told me to leave. I have become very aware of the wet soles of my boots and the small stone under one heel.
legacyText.1210480909: “She kept telling me not to drive in the snow,” he says.
legacyText.1999832709: I don't answer. I know something he hasn't asked me to know, and saying it would make me the owner of a conversation that belongs to him.
legacyText.2214962398: He looks at the envelope again.
legacyText.3832791763: “I was angry. I thought she didn't want help. She always made it sound like a nuisance, having somebody come over.”
legacyText.3059694594: Imani shifts beside me. Julian studies a crack in the step.
legacyText.1410102541: Martin rubs his thumb along the fold.
legacyText.1567611068: He goes inside. The door closes gently. I hear a chair move in the kitchen, then another voice, too low to understand.
legacyText.3171236884: On the pavement, I take out my notebook to mark the promise complete. My pen hovers above the page.
legacyText.2570018952: Julian says, “Don't write what he said.”
legacyText.565295211: I had been about to. Not from malice. It was a clue, a response, something that might help explain the system. I close the notebook and put it away.
legacyText.3529794191: Miso walks beside the garden wall. His paws make four precise prints in the new snow. I watch them until the next patch of cleared pavement makes them disappear.
legacyText.2330334401: At the corner, Imani buys three small buns from the bakery. Julian says he doesn't want one, then eats half before remembering he said that. I stand under the awning, eating warm bread while the delivery driver restacks his empty crates.
legacyText.2223302756: “Was it worth the time?” Julian asks.
legacyText.2590579327: I think of Mum in a room I haven't reached yet. The deadline. The narrow places a day can acquire when I'm afraid of using it badly.
legacyText.920168847: “I don't know how to count it.”
legacyText.526920332: He accepts that. I am grateful he doesn't tell me the answer should be obvious.
legacyText.2849798713: On my phone, the routing entry for Celia Bell changes. A small line of text appears beneath it: received without continuation.
legacyText.2905363094: I show Julian. He stops eating.
legacyText.185531280: “That,” he says, “is what the acknowledgement is supposed to look like.”
legacyText.1384498707: I write down those words. Not Martin's letter. Not his grief. Just the part the line has given me permission to see.
legacyText.3921912979: When I reach the annex, Leila is standing outside the door. She looks at the time, at the three of us, and then at the bag from the bakery.
legacyText.228163249: Imani hands her the last bun. My aunt eats half of it before asking for the report.
legacyText.682513202: Leila collects me from the service door of a building I could have walked past a hundred times. She has borrowed Dennis's car, an elderly hatchback with a child seat in the back and a packet of wet wipes in every available pocket.
legacyText.4206564184: “Dennis has grandchildren,” she explains when Imani asks.
legacyText.2243479818: Julian sits in the front. He has to hold a cardboard box in his lap because the passenger footwell is full of additional wet wipes. Miso stays inside the box with the flap partly open. Nobody has suggested he needs to hide; he seems to prefer being luggage to being questioned.
legacyText.1087407662: I am home before nine. The flat looks ordinary from the doorway. The chair I wedged under the handle is back at the kitchen table. The screw from the handle sits beside my laptop. Someone has laid the chemistry worksheet neatly on top of it, although I left it on a streetcar which crossed a river under the city.
legacyText.2891503965: Leila checks the rooms before letting me in. She uses a little mirror from her bag, turning it towards each corner. I want to ask how she knows what to look for. I want to go straight to bed and wake up yesterday.
legacyText.195807228: There is a note on the table.
legacyText.1960366067: “You have my face in the mirror. I'd like it back.”
legacyText.743520127: It is written in pencil. The letters have the careful shape of someone copying them from a sign.
legacyText.2357974584: Miso sniffs it, sneezes and climbs onto the windowsill.
legacyText.1625114928: I put the note under an empty glass.
legacyText.1013494437: Imani's dad arrives while Leila is making toast. He is broad-shouldered, tired, and wearing a work jacket with a rip at the cuff. He looks first at Imani, then at Leila, then at me. His eyes stop on the dressing at my elbow.
legacyText.885553488: “A situation at the building. I needed Imani to help {{firstName}} get out.”
legacyText.1864013545: I can see her searching for a statement that is accurate enough to survive. I used to think grown-ups had some private source of better explanations. Watching my aunt choose each word, I begin to suspect that a lot of adulthood is deciding how much trouble the next sentence will cause.
legacyText.4050021141: Imani's dad doesn't like the answer. He doesn't have time to stay and dislike it properly. He tells Imani to get her bag.
legacyText.2169455717: She says, “I need to come back later.”
legacyText.2737743971: “Selection is tomorrow. You told me that was important.”
legacyText.2880542110: “Then eat. Sleep. And answer your phone.”
legacyText.2085070520: She takes the toast Leila offers and wraps it in a paper towel. At the door she looks back at me, waiting for something.
legacyText.1913430417: I realise I haven't thanked her.
legacyText.150826816: She gives a short nod. It isn't quite the response I wanted, but I'm not sure what response I earned.
legacyText.3466098685: After she leaves, Julian telephones his college and says he has a family emergency. He doesn't stumble over the lie. When he catches me looking, he covers the receiver.
legacyText.853671481: “My manager won't write 'trapped in another realm' on a reference.”
legacyText.3930103391: Leila calls my school. I hear her say medical issue, family situation, expected back Monday. The office person asks a question that makes her close her eyes.
legacyText.3349928371: “No. We don't have an update about Nadia.”
legacyText.3438770552: I leave the kitchen before she can finish.
legacyText.1007370167: My room smells of the orange peel I left on the desk yesterday. The bed is unmade. A clean school shirt hangs from the wardrobe handle because Leila refuses to put away clothes I am perfectly capable of putting away myself. Everything in the room is arranged around a person who thought they knew how Friday would go.
legacyText.3299409808: I sit on the bed and take off my boots. My socks have dried stiff at the ankles.
legacyText.3976844669: In my phone's drafts is the last message I wrote to Mum. I open it.
legacyText.1864740654: “Leila bought the wrong cereal again. I know you'd say it's the same cereal in a different box. It isn't. I can tell.”
legacyText.482239459: There is no ending to the message. I always got stuck there. How do I say goodbye to an email address when I've spent months insisting I'm only saying see you later?
legacyText.4090635351: I delete nothing. I close the draft.
legacyText.1207452009: On the other side of the wall, Julian and Leila are talking quietly. I can make out my name, Voss's name, the word lower. A chair scrapes. I press my face into the pillow, angry at how tired I am.
legacyText.640395333: When I wake, someone has put a glass of water by the bed. The flat is silent except for Miso snoring on my clean shirt.
legacyText.2278085036: It is two in the afternoon.
legacyText.214398971: My phone contains a message from Imani: Don't do the important bit without telling me.
legacyText.4186035299: I lie there with the phone balanced on my chest. Then I reply: Haven't found the important bit yet.
legacyText.3728807778: By the time Imani returns, Leila has covered the kitchen table with paper. Hospital forms, archive printouts, pages copied from the notebook. She has weighed the corners down with tins because the radiator makes a draft she doesn't trust.
legacyText.1346237460: Julian has drawn a map on the back of a grocery receipt. It is not a reassuring map. Arrows lead into boxes labelled POSSIBLY STORAGE and DO NOT ASSUME STAIRS.
legacyText.3830287909: “I thought you worked there,” I say.
legacyText.2995312914: “I work in the part where we catalogue telephones.”
legacyText.2476592489: He turns the receipt over. On the other side, between onions and detergent, is a name written several times. Ruth Park.
legacyText.3139362068: “My sister,” he says before I ask. “I'm supposed to remember her wedding.”
legacyText.1408013576: “I traded a memory for access to an address book. I meant to give away a Wednesday afternoon. The person taking it said that was fine.”
legacyText.326338342: “I didn't specify which Wednesday. Or who I was with. Weddings aren't always on Saturdays.”
legacyText.2384222857: He folds the receipt so the name disappears.
legacyText.2089522566: Leila reaches for a pencil. “We're not bargaining with anyone.”
legacyText.2209381249: My aunt gives her the look she uses when a patient has found a treatment on the internet. Imani returns it without seeming especially concerned.
legacyText.2602636636: I open the ledger copy from Mrs. Bell's flat. Nadia's entry has two boxes: sender present and receiving witness. Voss's name appears in the second. There should be a signature underneath. Instead somebody has crossed the return line out.
legacyText.2021134410: Miso walks over the papers and sits beside it.
legacyText.3342326206: Julian leans close. The pencil work is difficult to separate from the ruled line beneath it. He follows the marks with the blunt end of his pen.
legacyText.590213564: The kitchen feels too warm. I pull at the collar of my coat, which I haven't taken off since waking.
legacyText.1940090788: “The lower station. But the route's been renamed. We need its first designation.”
legacyText.118841513: Leila shakes her head. “Adrian will tell you enough to make you do what he wants.”
legacyText.870485519: “He's the only person who's offered to talk.”
legacyText.3287755028: The words land where I intend them to. I'm not proud of the small relief that follows.
legacyText.3468471781: My aunt puts the pencil down. “He paid for the first equipment. He designed most of the line controls. Your mother needed a way to hold two incompatible signals apart, and he had spent half his working life solving exactly that kind of problem. At first it was useful.”
legacyText.2921975917: Leila's eyes narrow. “How do you know that?”
legacyText.3417121632: I show her the photograph from the cupboard, which Julian brought in his box. The girl in the yellow coat stands beside a woman whose face has been cut out of the picture.
legacyText.784529161: “Eva,” Leila says. “His wife left him after the funeral. Don't invent a story about that. I don't know why she left.”
legacyText.1156738245: Imani picks up one of the printouts. It is a donor report, neatly formatted, with Voss's full name and the date Nadia stopped signing the weekly test sheets.
legacyText.2337573979: “Eleven months,” she says. “Why is it starting now?”
legacyText.1489636753: Then Julian takes the bell diagram and turns it ninety degrees. The twelve scratches around its edge align with twelve smaller marks in Mum's circuit.
legacyText.550500672: “They're holding intervals. Not months exactly. Load cycles.”
legacyText.2349190326: He draws a thirteenth mark. It crosses all the others.
legacyText.3502219996: “When the last interval closes, every waiting message tries to complete at the same time.”
legacyText.3299988453: I think of the boy with the bread. The woman waiting on the platform. The person wearing my face.
legacyText.1491535201: Julian doesn't write a number. He puts his pen down.
legacyText.1722805650: I take my phone out before anybody can tell me not to. Voss's message is still there. This time it displays a number. I press call.
legacyText.3106647119: He answers on the second ring.
legacyText.593676643: “Good. I'd prefer she heard this too.”
legacyText.2662672855: That is an intelligent thing to say. I dislike him a little more for saying it.
legacyText.140203538: “Alive. I spoke to her this morning.”
legacyText.324088038: Leila holds out a hand. I don't give her the phone.
legacyText.3845451010: “I can't from here. I can show you the direct line. But I need you to come to the gallery on Harbord. Four o'clock. Public place. Bring whoever you need to feel comfortable.”
legacyText.1722907202: The cat doesn't look away from the phone.
legacyText.1688174954: Voss continues. “You'll hear some very alarming things about me. Several are true. Ask yourself why nobody else has brought your mother home.”
legacyText.286688411: Imani watches me set the phone down. “He's good at that.”
legacyText.2424069078: I want to tell her I'm not stupid. Instead I look at the timetable on her screen, which she has been checking between sentences. Saturday morning. A rink address. A time in bold.
legacyText.1502736336: “Because you keep saying it like I don't.”
legacyText.3261327736: She takes the receipt map and puts it inside her phone case. It is a small practical act, and the argument I was preparing has nowhere sensible to go.
legacyText.443232440: At the bottom of one routing sheet, a note specifies that diverted calls carry the next reserved receiving date, not the time of the speaker. I copy it because it may explain tomorrow on my phone. It does not yet explain whose voice I heard.
legacyText.1202169400: My friend Ella messages while Julian is sorting the gallery numbers. She sends a photograph of the chemistry board, followed by a second photograph because the first is blurred.
legacyText.790489345: I haven't replied to her last four messages. I meant to. At first I didn't know what to say. Then replying required explaining why I hadn't replied, and the explanation became another message I couldn't finish.
legacyText.1618600124: Now she writes: “Your aunt said medical. You okay?”
legacyText.669353474: I type yes, delete it, and type: At home. Family thing. Thanks for the notes.
legacyText.624572599: “You don't have to do a whole update. Just send a full stop sometimes so I know you're not dead.”
legacyText.3374853863: I stare at the screen. The word dead looks different when someone uses it carelessly. It also looks like a word a friend might use because she has no idea how to ask the careful question without sounding like everybody else.
legacyText.3789045014: Her reply comes immediately: Incredible. Communication.
legacyText.2588679488: I laugh before remembering I am supposed to be frightened. It is a small sound, but Julian looks up.
legacyText.1585007197: I take the phone into the sitting room and call her. She answers with, “Oh. A voice. Didn't know yours still worked.”
legacyText.2592981446: She tells me about school. Someone has moved my locker contents because the hinge broke again. My chemistry teacher has decided to give everyone an extra week on the project, which Ella calls a personal apology from the universe. A boy I don't particularly like has been saying things about my attendance. She tells me she dealt with it, then refuses to specify how.
legacyText.611703531: For several minutes I am allowed to be irritated by the correct small things. I sit on the floor beside the sofa and pick at a loose thread while she complains about the cafeteria's attempt at soup.
legacyText.698203376: Then she says, “Someone rang my mum last night. Asked for you.”
legacyText.3309796964: “Didn't say. Mum thought it was school. At three in the morning, so obviously not school, but you know how people sound official and she starts finding a pen.”
legacyText.1816481966: “Your full name. Whether she knew where you were.”
legacyText.4169944643: There is a pause. “I don't think so. Why?”
legacyText.454998595: I go to the kitchen door and beckon Julian. He sees my face and puts his papers down.
legacyText.1248301970: “I need you to ask her. Don't call the number back.”
legacyText.4029590829: “I know it sounds strange. Please don't call it back.”
legacyText.1935024951: Ella goes quiet in a way that is worse than a question. I hear her walk into another room and speak to her mother. The answer comes through indistinctly. Then Ella returns.
legacyText.2362497027: “She said she didn't know. She told them to call your aunt.”
legacyText.1216996043: Julian holds out a scrap of paper. On it he has written: If they have a voice, they try its connections.
legacyText.2677728719: I think of my unanswered messages. The group chat. A person asking after I because she wants me to show up in class, accidentally becoming a line the Exchange can use.
legacyText.2724451575: “I can't explain all of it yet,” I say. “Something happened with Mum's work. Somebody is trying to get information through people who know us.”
legacyText.3107549485: That is true enough to sound worse than the version involving a talking cat.
legacyText.898535588: Leila has come in behind Julian. I pass her the phone. She gives Ella a number for Dennis, then says the calls are part of an ongoing safety problem and should not be answered. She doesn't tell Ella she imagined anything. I hear the care in that choice.
legacyText.1301517579: Afterwards, Ella asks for me back.
legacyText.3250851810: “You could've told me there was a problem.”
legacyText.2974761346: “I didn't ask for a perfect explanation.”
legacyText.2042256765: I sit down again. The loose thread has wrapped around one finger so tightly it has left a red line.
legacyText.1112906765: She tells me she will keep the notes. If I need to miss another week, say so. If I don't want people asking questions, say that too. She doesn't promise to make everyone behave. She does promise to send a full stop at lunch.
legacyText.3683868486: I agree to send one back.
legacyText.121837968: When the call ends, Julian adds Ella's household to the map. He writes only the information needed to block the diverted request, then puts the rest of the page facedown.
legacyText.2224267811: I recognise the distinction from Mrs. Bell's letter.
legacyText.3807359960: “I don't want everyone I know pulled into this.”
legacyText.1391249579: “Then we give the line fewer ways to mistake concern for permission.”
legacyText.2378313691: He shows me how to mark a receiving refusal on an ordinary piece of paper, tied to a number rather than a person. Leila calls Ella's mother and talks her through it as an unusual precaution. I can hear how odd the instructions sound. I can also hear the other woman deciding to do them anyway.
legacyText.2520766095: For the next twenty minutes I copy the mark onto cards for the households Leila knows have received calls. It is repetitive work. My hand gets tired. Nothing dramatic happens.
legacyText.2394272477: When one of the lines on Julian's map goes dark, I keep working.
legacyText.822840478: The gallery sells landscape paintings and very expensive lamps. Through the window I can see a blue lake rendered in thick paint, with a small red canoe positioned to make the blue seem bigger. I spend a moment wondering whether the painter has ever been in a canoe before remembering that I have come to confront a man about my missing mother.
legacyText.2016460333: Voss is waiting at a table near the back. He gets up when I enter.
legacyText.2021105730: He looks ordinary. This annoys me. His coat is hung neatly on the chair. His shirt has a pale stain near one cuff. There is a loose thread on his scarf which he keeps trying to tuck out of sight.
legacyText.4168027203: She says it before I can decide whether refusing tea makes me look more suspicious than accepting it.
legacyText.2720283927: Leila stands behind my chair. Miso has refused to enter the gallery, which Voss notices without asking about. I can see the cat through the window, sitting beside a planter and watching a pigeon with excessive concentration.
legacyText.1316568238: Voss takes a small device from his bag. It looks like a dictation recorder with a brass socket fitted into its side.
legacyText.3502218007: “Your mother's line. One-way for now. She won't hear you.”
legacyText.3563512538: I look at Leila. She nods, reluctantly.
legacyText.2641959028: Mum is humming. Very badly. A tune I remember because she never got past the same four notes. Something clicks. She says, “No, that won't hold,” then swears softly enough that I have to lean closer.
legacyText.839170832: I cover the lower half of my face with one hand.
legacyText.3062958237: Leila reaches for the device. Voss lets her inspect it. She listens, checks a tiny movement in the brass socket and sets it back down.
legacyText.3844015435: Mum hums the four notes again.
legacyText.1378094540: “The lower station,” Voss says. “She made herself part of the holding circuit. I have a way to relieve her.”
legacyText.1476152391: The woman at the front of the gallery glances over. Voss lowers his voice.
legacyText.4274269180: I look at him properly for the first time.
legacyText.567120200: He lets the silence sit. He is very good at leaving a space I want to fill for him.
legacyText.4185132175: “The station won't accept the person who diverted its first return line. There needs to be a witness to alter that restriction. A relative of the person holding it would be strongest.”
legacyText.2888366668: Voss smiles at her without showing his teeth. “Yes.”
legacyText.1588713990: Leila leans forward. “You told Nadia the acknowledgement controls were manual. She trusted you.”
legacyText.3460322322: He looks down at the loose thread on his scarf. For a moment the mild expression slips.
legacyText.2637230567: The room stays quiet. On the recorder Mum says a number, corrects it and starts over. I know how she sounds when she has been working too long. She is there now.
legacyText.3227124444: “The little girl. That's who you're trying to bring back.”
legacyText.931648374: His hand closes around the edge of the table.
legacyText.223830275: Leila puts a hand on my shoulder. I move out from under it without thinking. Voss sees that too.
legacyText.670593663: He takes a photograph from his wallet. Eva stands in the raincoat, front tooth missing, holding a small snow globe. The woman cut out of the other picture is present in this one, her arm around Eva's shoulders. She looks tired and happy and not like an explanation for anything.
legacyText.3517092531: “She hated snow,” he says. “Until it stopped. Then she wanted it back. Every year.”
legacyText.3243582057: “I heard her through one of Nadia's early tests. Just a word. My name.”
legacyText.756388454: “Did she ask you to do this?”
legacyText.2534458323: It is the wrong question, and it still works. I look towards the recorder.
legacyText.3837623329: Voss pushes a card across the table. On it is an address and a time: lower entrance, six p.m. He has written the time by hand.
legacyText.2866855527: “You can investigate without me. I expect you will. But I have access she needs. Don't let somebody else's account of me cost you another chance.”
legacyText.2017792062: Outside, Miso is standing with all four paws planted against the pavement.
legacyText.726322324: Voss follows my gaze. “Ask him about the collar. Ask whose name keeps it closed.”
legacyText.370540280: Mum's voice stops. I reach for the recorder before I can stop myself.
legacyText.2110317792: He gets up, pays for four cups of tea nobody ordered, and leaves through a side door.
legacyText.4147034865: For a while I sit with the photograph he forgot on the table. Then Leila turns it over.
legacyText.2296923039: On the back, under Eva's name, is a short list of numbers. One has been crossed out and replaced. I copy all of them.
legacyText.77202553: Imani notices. She says nothing until we're outside.
legacyText.679949009: It is a different answer. I keep it to myself instead of making a joke.
legacyText.2368247318: Julian finds the first number from Voss's photograph in a disconnected catalogue. It refers to a room the archive no longer owns, in a building demolished before I was born.
legacyText.1759379666: She waits for the rest of that sentence. Julian takes off his cardigan and puts it back on as if that will make the explanation easier.
legacyText.1191240983: “Addresses don't disappear at the same speed as buildings.”
legacyText.1466026965: Miso leads me through the back of a laundrette. The owner looks up from folding towels, sees Julian and says, “If you're going downstairs, bring up my trolley.”
legacyText.2912711650: Julian promises to try. Outside the basement door he stops me.
legacyText.3481226591: “I'm not promising anything else in there. I've already lost enough.”
legacyText.36406440: The stairs end in a market built from shelves. High above me, light falls through a roof of catalogue cards. People move along narrow aisles with bags held close to their chests. A man is selling keys without teeth. A woman has arranged glasses of water around a notebook. Every time she turns a page, someone whispers through the glasses.
legacyText.2679439439: I keep my hands in my pockets.
legacyText.1792673228: At the centre stands a desk broad enough to eat dinner on. Behind it a man with a long, narrow face is writing in three books at once. His left hand turns a page. His right continues writing. A third pen moves without anyone holding it.
legacyText.904326038: Miso sits at a respectful distance.
legacyText.3365277328: The man doesn't look up. “The trolley's behind the north shelves, Julian.”
legacyText.3762672955: “You were going to. And your earlier request remains under review.”
legacyText.3240135056: I put the copied number on the desk. The third pen stops.
legacyText.1630991879: “A diverted address,” the man says. “Whose permission do you bring to examine it?”
legacyText.4083855292: I look at the notebook. Mum wrote my name in it. She told me to find Leila. She didn't tell me to come here.
legacyText.4006168044: “Then tell me whose permission you bring.”
legacyText.2285695631: The man draws a line under my number. When he turns his head, his shadow on the shelf has a long curved beak. I remember a school project, a picture of an ibis, my mother's patient explanation that the gods had more than one form and people should stop treating the heads like a matching quiz.
legacyText.1992746119: “Among other ways of asking for my attention.”
legacyText.1560357892: “You need access to the record of its alteration. Those are different requests.”
legacyText.1513455293: Imani rests her hands on the edge of the desk. “What do we have to pay?”
legacyText.3146251806: “It becomes less vague if you stop offering me objects I have no use for.”
legacyText.218539451: I hadn't offered him anything. He looks towards the notebook under my arm, and I tuck it closer before I can help myself.
legacyText.3663594730: Thoth sets one of the three books in front of me. In the first column are names. In the second, brief statements. In the third, the spaces where signatures should be.
legacyText.2999528948: NADIA {{surname|upper}}. EXTENDED VOLUNTARY SERVICE. AUTHORITY TO DELEGATE RECEIPT.
legacyText.522256189: The signature underneath resembles my mother's. It is too tidy. Mum always let the last stroke trail into whatever space was left. This version stops exactly where the ruled box ends.
legacyText.1218136970: I take out the letter from Mrs. Bell's flat. The ledger copy. Mum's recording. On their own they explain pieces. Together they show who was present, who changed the route and when my mother stopped signing.
legacyText.2931223458: Thoth listens to the recording without expression. When Mum swears at the battery cover, the third pen makes a small mark in its book.
legacyText.1126250705: “You can file these,” he says. “They will be retained until the dispute is settled.”
legacyText.1097456107: I hold the recorder tighter. It has her voice on it. I only just got it.
legacyText.847793408: Julian puts his own recorder beside mine.
legacyText.2184068673: I could trust the process. I could try to steal the book and run, though every aisle looks the same and the person behind the desk has been turning pages without using his hands. I could refuse the terms and try Voss's lower entrance, knowing less about what he plans.
legacyText.2601041463: Thoth waits. He doesn't make the decision easier by being kind.
legacyText.2767494968: Behind me, a trolley rolls slowly out of a side aisle and nudges Julian's ankle.
legacyText.3297833328: “Ask me for something I can return,” Thoth tells him.
legacyText.2805728961: Julian looks down at the handle. For a moment I think he's going to argue. Instead he takes the trolley and pushes it towards the stairs.
legacyText.279207389: I look back at the disputed signature. Mum's name shouldn't be sitting in a book beside a sentence she never agreed to.
legacyText.1412230070: I keep one hand on the recorder while I decide.
legacyText.1919613135: Imani taps the place where I copied the numbers. “You said there was nothing else. Next time tell me before the locked door.”
legacyText.3244131031: The correction doesn't make the lie disappear. Thoth rules a narrow line through it, leaving every letter legible, and attaches a reference number to the evidence.
legacyText.1369384782: “People will still be able to see it?” I ask.
legacyText.2827122295: “They need to see what was changed.”
legacyText.3524128473: He writes a second address beneath the first. The marks look simple until I try to copy them. One seems to belong behind another, although they're both on the same page.
legacyText.490930330: I make six small numbered boxes. Thoth watches me fill them.
legacyText.2166001151: “Take the witness receipt,” he says. “You may challenge a delegated authority once. It will not hold the door open for you. It will make the door ask the question it was told to skip.”
legacyText.3544408518: I fold the receipt along its printed line. It is longer than my pocket, so I fold it twice more. Nobody says anything about the untidy result.
legacyText.732955663: The address on the public card takes longer to copy than I expect. Without a witness seal, every redirected mark has to be checked against the notebook. Julian helps without claiming I have proof I chose not to submit. I write the missing receipt on a separate line so nobody can mistake the address for one.
legacyText.554660892: On the way out, Imani buys a bottle of water from the laundrette. Ordinary water, from an ordinary fridge, with an ordinary price she objects to before paying it. Julian helps carry the trolley up the stairs. The owner says, “Finally,” and gives him a packet of biscuits.
legacyText.2988024440: We sit on the laundrette's front step and pass the biscuits between us. It is nearly six. The sky has the flat purple colour it gets before snow, and the bus shelter across the road is crowded with people trying not to touch.
legacyText.1813858776: Julian takes one biscuit, then breaks it and puts half back.
legacyText.2168114483: I turn towards him. He keeps looking at the road.
legacyText.841411689: “About the wedding. I let her think I was drunk. The photographer sent me the pictures. I know where everyone stood. I can describe the cake.”
legacyText.1915598538: “It makes me better at lying about it.”
legacyText.4261443397: The laundrette door opens behind me. Warm air and the smell of soap spill over the steps. A woman carries a bag past me without looking down.
legacyText.1881977606: Imani asks, “What did you need the address book for?”
legacyText.905400726: Julian rubs the biscuit crumbs off his hand.
legacyText.2628147503: “Nadia. After she disappeared. I thought I could find her before anybody noticed how much I didn't know.”
legacyText.707762119: I hadn't expected that. I thought he would say a rare book, or a promotion, or a door he shouldn't have tried. Something that would make the price easier to judge.
legacyText.2074963612: “I didn't know you,” he adds. “It wasn't for you.”
legacyText.1847774696: “She took me seriously. At work. That's all.”
legacyText.1376090696: He says that's all in a tone that makes Imani stop asking questions.
legacyText.1268838838: Miso is crouched under the step, watching a delivery cyclist fix a dropped chain. His collar has appeared around his neck. I haven't seen it before. Thin black leather, too tight at the throat, with a brass plate tucked under the fur.
legacyText.67570247: “Voss tells everybody something true when he wants them to stop noticing the rest.”
legacyText.1926719793: Miso stands and walks towards the alley. I get up after him.
legacyText.1411891354: He moves faster. I follow him around the corner, leaving Imani and Julian on the step.
legacyText.631848936: At the end of the alley, he turns.
legacyText.4024967127: “Opening doors. Carrying messages. Finding people he said were lost.”
legacyText.1038836255: The question hangs there long enough to answer itself.
legacyText.4021262546: I sit back on a low wall. My elbow throbs where the dressing pulls against the cut.
legacyText.4038510107: “Did she know you worked for him?”
legacyText.2939696728: A rubbish bag shifts in the wind. Miso watches it instead of me.
legacyText.328023639: I have to put my hands somewhere. I push them under my arms.
legacyText.828121837: He raises his head. Under the brass plate, his fur has worn away in a narrow strip.
legacyText.1706201618: “I don't get to tell every truth I know,” he says. “I can tell you this one because you brought it out of his mouth and put it into yours. Ask me something else about him and see what happens.”
legacyText.3466663258: I don't. I'm not willing to test the collar by hurting him just to see whether he's honest.
legacyText.4093345964: Imani appears at the corner. She stops when she sees our faces.
legacyText.3600394497: “Julian's got a message from Leila. Bell's getting worse. She says if we're using that address, we go now.”
legacyText.3851444136: Miso walks past her without speaking. I wait until he has gone, then show Imani the photograph I copied at the gallery. The list of numbers on the back. The part I hadn't told anybody about because I wanted to be the person with something useful.
legacyText.1366662590: She studies the page. Then she looks at me. “You said there wasn't anything else.” I start to explain about checking it. She gives the notebook back carefully. “Tell me what I'm walking into before I'm already there.”
legacyText.2899706468: She compares the page with the copy she made at the gallery. “Same sequence,” she says. “Good. We can stop checking one another's handwriting.” She hands the notebook back with the relevant page still open.
legacyText.2308951794: I put the page where everyone can see it when I return to the step.
legacyText.3583271733: The return address does not open on the first attempt. Julian checks my copied marks against the witness receipt, then against the number on Voss's photograph.
legacyText.2033762010: “He can make the line take a different way.”
legacyText.540495281: Miso sniffs the bottom of the wall. Water has begun to seep through a crack in the skirting board. It pools around his paws and reflects a ceiling the exchange room doesn't have.
legacyText.491868353: Julian grabs the equipment box. Imani takes my sleeve. The water rises in a sheet, climbing away from the floor until it stands between us and the booths.
legacyText.3623421805: On the other side, the reflected ceiling becomes a long throat.
legacyText.111430477: I make a sound I won't later describe as a scream. Imani pulls me behind the desk as the water collapses where I was standing. It strikes the floor hard enough to split a tile.
legacyText.905623637: Miso is already on a shelf. His ears are flat. Julian has the notebook open with one hand and is trying to protect the paper with the other.
legacyText.182164072: A shape gathers inside the water, narrow at the front, thickening along the floor. It moves like a snake, except the surface keeps showing things behind me. My kitchen. A hospital corridor. The underside of Mum's table.
legacyText.158901065: I remember pictures of the great serpent opposing the sun's nightly passage. The thing on the floor is much smaller, assembled out of borrowed reflections and a bad instruction. That does not make its approach feel manageable.
legacyText.2896398087: Julian finds a note in Mum's manual.
legacyText.2444975993: All three of us look at my phone.
legacyText.3179835304: I turn it off. The water keeps coming.
legacyText.1286389964: The blue notebook is warm under my arm. I take it out and the leading edge turns towards it.
legacyText.3550789391: Mum's address. My connection to her. The thing isn't choosing me because I'm important. It is taking the shortest available route.
legacyText.3289001128: I put the notebook on the desk and step away. The water follows it, gathering against the wooden legs.
legacyText.3006069190: Imani looks at the high shelf near the wall. “Can it climb?”
legacyText.4009924930: As if answering, the water begins to climb.
legacyText.2820692217: Julian passes me the chalk. “Hold the connection between it and the address. Don't try to hold all the water.”
legacyText.3220804733: I kneel behind the desk. The floor is wet. The first line dissolves before I finish it.
legacyText.2046447250: Imani tears a page from the back of an old catalogue and puts it on a dry part of the desk. I draw the mark there. It is harder with my hands shaking. I close the circle and give it a definite subject: route to address, not address to person.
legacyText.3888376584: Miso jumps to the top of the wall, where a pipe passes through a hole larger than it needs to be. He scratches at the plaster. On the other side, a narrow staircase appears, leading down past the telephone booths.
legacyText.1554820867: “Empty channel,” he says. “Can you send it there?”
legacyText.2165685275: “Not if we close it before the next arrival.”
legacyText.3616312569: That is not a completely reassuring answer. I think of the boy with the bread and the platforms where people wait. I don't want to push a danger out of sight and call it solved.
legacyText.92923269: Julian studies the address on the notebook.
legacyText.1783727735: “We can use an unassigned return. No receiver. Then close both ends.”
legacyText.3577655024: He shows me the open stroke on the temporary hold, then turns the page so I can see how the route should finish. I have to move the mark, not break it. If I erase the wrong side, the water will return to the strongest signal. I.
legacyText.2158770775: Imani puts the notebook inside the equipment box and slides the box towards the staircase. The water turns. I move the chalk line a little at a time, opening one end only after the next has been drawn.
legacyText.2582942458: My hand cramps. The water trembles. I tell Imani to stop moving and wait until I can feel my fingers again.
legacyText.3015875570: She waits. It matters more than any encouragement she could have shouted.
legacyText.564695641: At the staircase, the route narrows to a stream. The rest of the room drains into it with a sound like a bathtub emptying through a wall.
legacyText.1915857095: Julian counts down from three. I close the far end. He closes the near one.
legacyText.2088658582: For a moment nobody moves. Then the desk collapses, one leg giving way where the first impact cracked it. The notebook slides out of the box and lands at my feet, dry except along one corner.
legacyText.4204514043: Imani sits down on a chair that has survived and bends over her knees. Julian wipes the floor with a towel so he can examine the broken route without stepping in it. Miso climbs down from the wall, misses the last shelf and pretends he meant to land that loudly.
legacyText.2345542766: In the margin beside the return address, Mum has written a small instruction I hadn't understood before: Do not confuse connection with appetite.
legacyText.2937532262: I add my own note underneath.
legacyText.2375703027: It isn't elegant. I think she will know what I mean.
legacyText.2359662541: The green door appears in the wall where I first tried the address. Through its wire-glass window, a woman sits at a table.
legacyText.3902422640: I stand up so fast the chair behind me falls over.
legacyText.716707893: The address opens a door in the wall of the exchange room. I know the wall was blank because I helped Julian carry a shelving unit away from it. Now it has a green door with a brass number and a wire-glass window.
legacyText.625042904: Behind the glass, my mother is sitting at a table.
legacyText.51103152: For several seconds I don't move. She looks thinner. Her hair is cut unevenly above her shoulders, with one piece tucked behind an ear. There is a mug near her elbow. She keeps reaching for it and putting it down again without drinking.
legacyText.1356934368: I say, “Mum,” but there is no sound. My mouth has done the shape and forgotten the rest.
legacyText.3114813706: Imani puts a hand against my back.
legacyText.691326694: Her chair falls over when she stands. I see her take two steps towards the door, then stop as a cable stretched across the table pulls tight. Her right hand is wrapped around it. The skin across her fingers is red and raw.
legacyText.291028348: I nod, then realise how absurd that is. She can see my face. I should say something, tell her I brought help, tell her Leila is waiting, tell her I didn't throw away the blue mug when its handle broke.
legacyText.2954453913: What comes out is, “I did my homework.”
legacyText.192322598: Mum puts her free hand over her mouth. For a moment she looks like she might laugh. Then she starts crying, silently, with her eyes still fixed on me.
legacyText.3859273063: Julian opens the door just far enough to pass a piece of chalk through. He keeps one foot against the bottom.
legacyText.2617468271: “There's a load on the threshold,” he says. “We need something to hold it.”
legacyText.3552581315: I kneel and draw the mark. My first circle comes out lopsided. I rub it away with my sleeve and start again. Forty-one seconds in the exchange room wasn't enough. I need longer now. I close the last line and tell the chalk exactly which connection I intend to hold: door, frame, this side, that side.
legacyText.3818728061: The green paint goes pale. Julian pushes. The gap widens.
legacyText.3765233083: Imani braces her stick against the wall and slides through first. I follow her into a room that smells of dust and hot wiring.
legacyText.3325817662: Mum is close enough to touch.
legacyText.3158322328: I don't run at her. I think I might break something if I do. I walk carefully around a chair and take her free hand.
legacyText.2622678079: It is warm. There is a hard patch on the side of her middle finger where she always held a pen. I press my thumb against it, needing proof more precise than her face.
legacyText.1786945744: She pulls me against her shoulder.
legacyText.1910295809: I make a sound that hurts my throat. Her free arm tightens around me. I would like the next minute to be uncomplicated. I would like at least that much.
legacyText.849343033: The cable jerks. Mum gasps and lets me go.
legacyText.3159670979: Julian is standing beside the table, reading the labels on a panel. “We can relieve the hand control. Where's the second reader?”
legacyText.376958342: Imani holds the door. “We have six minutes.”
legacyText.2211250348: I look at Mum's hand. The cable passes through a loop of brass fitted around her wrist. It isn't tied. The loop has closed into itself.
legacyText.1310308951: She says it too quickly, then catches herself.
legacyText.3866001757: “Listen. It's carrying people. Messages with the connections still attached. If we cut indiscriminately, the damage travels back to the living end.”
legacyText.3141296154: The room becomes quiet except for a relay clicking under the table.
legacyText.2990978577: Mum points to a row of labels. Three are blank.
legacyText.3554199427: “I didn't know who they belonged to until they went blank.”
legacyText.523315561: I want to argue that she couldn't know, that this isn't her fault. But I don't know enough yet to tell her what belongs to her and what doesn't. I hold her free hand instead.
legacyText.2124955793: Julian finds a second connector behind the panel. “It's still here. He removed the receiver, not the socket.”
legacyText.1344518957: For a second I can hear breathing from everywhere, too many people sharing too little air. Then a child's voice speaks through the wall.
legacyText.4010560933: “Dad says you can't take her yet.”
legacyText.2882796421: Imani pulls me backwards as the table shifts. One leg sinks through the floor. Mum reaches for me with her free hand, misses, catches my coat.
legacyText.3669197522: The seam by the bird patch tears.
legacyText.2140305062: Miso leaps onto the panel. His claws scrape metal. Julian is trying to pull the connector free, but his hand has gone rigid. I see the skin on his wrist turning grey.
legacyText.2382179307: There is time to reach one of them before the door closes. Mum is standing. Julian isn't moving. Imani's stick has begun to bend against the frame.
legacyText.69190447: Leila doesn't ask whether I found Nadia. She sees me carrying Julian and opens the fire door wider.
legacyText.329726482: I sit him in a chair. His hand is grey to the wrist, the fingers stiff and curled. Imani puts the broken hockey stick against the wall. The blade has separated along one layer, leaving a thin splinter that she keeps touching with her thumb.
legacyText.3689772780: She asks the same questions twice more, then turns to Miso.
legacyText.188410365: Miso's tail moves sharply once. “You touched the free connector.”
legacyText.4283554876: Leila looks at the cat. He stops talking.
legacyText.840700339: I stand near the coffee stain, which someone has put a wet-floor sign over instead of cleaning. I keep seeing Mum reach for me. Her hand closing on the coat. The patch tearing. I could have held on longer. I know the door was closing. I could still have tried.
legacyText.3248884750: Leila finishes wrapping Julian's hand in loose cloth, then comes to me.
legacyText.4147686590: I push up my sleeve. The dressing has soaked through.
legacyText.3780695318: She looks at the cut and goes still in the careful way that means she is trying not to react. Then she takes my arm gently and washes it.
legacyText.3320000273: “I know she was there. I don't know what it was like. Tell me.”
legacyText.1154509324: I look at the top of her head. Her hair is going grey near the parting. I haven't noticed that before, though it must have been happening in the same flat I live in.
legacyText.753447727: Leila presses her lips together. I try to explain the cable, the panel, the part of Mum's hand I held. None of it comes in the right order. Leila doesn't correct me. When she tapes the clean dressing down, her fingers are shaking.
legacyText.3368952184: The question has been waiting for eleven months. Now that I know she's alive, it feels harder to ask.
legacyText.4157126440: Miso answers from beside Julian's chair.
legacyText.3658268516: “Every outside call has a cost. The first ones went to people Adrian chose. After she realised, she stopped trying.”
legacyText.855527739: I look at the phone in my hand. Friday, nine forty-seven p.m. The unknown call is listed at two thirteen. Tomorrow's date has returned beside it.
legacyText.4067128020: Julian has stopped moving his grey fingers.
legacyText.1080759099: “The return line isn't just misdirected,” he says. “It's carrying an instruction. You can't pull her out while that instruction still names her as the receiver.”
legacyText.3732193582: I hear the idea before I admit it's mine. My name. My hand on the cable. Mum walking out. There must be a way to stand where she is until somebody fixes it properly. I could learn enough. I've already learned more today than I thought possible.
legacyText.1308549802: Imani gets up to leave. I turn towards her, suddenly afraid she has had enough. She lifts her damaged stick.
legacyText.1701974438: “I have to be at the rink at ten. My dad's taking me. If I don't sleep now I might as well not go.”
legacyText.3483973837: I almost ask how she can think about hockey. Then I see the tape worn smooth where her glove rests, the careful way she avoids putting weight on the damaged blade.
legacyText.159597436: She puts on her coat. At the door she says, “You should come. Not for the hockey. Just get out of here for an hour.”
legacyText.3374125155: I look towards the bell cupboard.
legacyText.3760363928: “It won't all happen because you sat down,” she says.
legacyText.836436738: After she leaves, Leila makes me eat soup from a paper cup. It is too hot. I drink it anyway, standing near Julian while he uses his good hand to redraw the connector he couldn't reach.
legacyText.3894836135: At the bottom of the drawing, beside the receiver slot, he writes one word.
legacyText.4041745112: Then he crosses it out and writes: REMOVAL OF REFUSAL.
legacyText.1500130208: I fold the page carefully. This time I know which question to bring back.
legacyText.1467179505: I wake to somebody knocking on a metal door and spend several seconds trying to remember which side I'm on.
legacyText.3708313002: Then I recognise the annex storeroom. Leila has made a bed from two coats and a camping mat Dennis found in his car. Julian is asleep in the chair, his bandaged hand supported by a rolled towel. Miso occupies the warm patch under the radiator.
legacyText.2484995789: The knocking is Dennis. He has brought porridge, four plastic spoons and a large piece of paper on which he has written EMERGENCY CONTACTS in capital letters.
legacyText.1525847110: “Somebody ought to know where everybody is,” he says.
legacyText.3965947174: I eat the porridge. It tastes of the inside of the cardboard tub. When I check my phone, Imani has sent the rink address with no explanation.
legacyText.843169331: Leila sees me put my boots on.
legacyText.2903638080: She looks at the clock, then at the bell cupboard. The holding mark has been renewed so many times that white dust covers the hinges.
legacyText.2026095491: I nod. It is a smaller request. I can manage it.
legacyText.1047690587: The rink smells of old rubber and cold air. Parents lean against the barrier holding paper cups. Someone is arguing about a helmet. Through the glass, skaters move between cones while a coach points at something I can't identify.
legacyText.3149926635: Imani is near the goal, wearing a helmet with a white scratch across the front. I hadn't realised how much equipment she needs to stand there. Her gloves look enormous. The substitute stick is dark green, with tape peeling from the shaft.
legacyText.1804177896: Her dad spots me and lifts his chin in greeting.
legacyText.149128241: He watches Imani stop a shot, then says, “She nervous?”
legacyText.517629784: I have no advice for him. He seems content not to receive any.
legacyText.1964534589: For twenty minutes nothing supernatural happens. Nobody's reflection moves incorrectly. The scoreboard displays a sensible number. A child drops a mitten down the gap behind a bench and becomes much more upset than the situation seems to warrant, until I remember I don't know what else happened to them today.
legacyText.3825256284: Imani misses a shot. Her dad shifts his weight. I glance at him, but he is smiling slightly.
legacyText.3518757361: “Too far out,” he says, to himself.
legacyText.4275270316: I watch the next shot closely enough to see what he means. The puck goes left, Imani moves, the glove closes. Her dad taps the barrier with two fingers. She doesn't look over.
legacyText.4058367613: Julian: Found a maintenance entry. Maybe a way around the witness circuit. Need original operator manual.
legacyText.1379316885: Might be in the flat. Don't go without Leila.
legacyText.576876461: I look at the rink doors. I could leave now and be at the flat before the session ends. I know where Mum kept her manuals. Imani wouldn't notice until she came off the ice.
legacyText.2631581654: On the far side of the glass, she looks towards the benches. Her helmet turns just enough for me to know she's seen me.
legacyText.3061156814: The flat is colder than I remember. Leila goes straight to the radiator and turns the valve, then checks the mirror by the front door before allowing anyone to take off a coat.
legacyText.330120942: Imani goes to the kitchen. Julian checks the window latch. Miso stays on the threshold, making a point of waiting until I look at him.
legacyText.1014444036: Mum's manuals are on the bottom shelf in the sitting room. I used to build little walls around them with my schoolbooks because she complained when I stacked anything heavy on top. Most are ordinary repair guides, full of parts diagrams and warnings about electricity. The one I need has no title on its spine.
legacyText.1883311874: Inside, someone has written a list of names. I recognise Nadia, Adrian, Celia. The fourth is Leila's.
legacyText.3633142665: I bring the book into the kitchen.
legacyText.4246926491: My aunt has filled the kettle. She turns it off before it boils.
legacyText.2661756775: “I witnessed the first tests,” she says.
legacyText.1922367982: She looks at the open page instead of defending herself.
legacyText.2068061639: “There were people at the hospital who died before someone could get there. Nadia wanted to know whether something could be done about that.”
legacyText.4050231147: “Some did. We asked. We wrote it down. Not everybody said yes.”
legacyText.1489328855: I turn the page. Beside several names, in my aunt's compact handwriting, is the word declined. No explanation. No attempt to talk them round.
legacyText.1119170455: Julian sets his bandaged hand on the table. Leila looks at it and closes her eyes briefly.
legacyText.3776653521: “Adrian wanted the line to stay open after a refusal. He said someone might change their mind. Nadia said they could make a new call.”
legacyText.3479947172: “I thought a delay could be harmless if nobody received anything until they agreed.”
legacyText.740890377: I wait. She rubs one thumb against the other.
legacyText.4024233: “I signed off on a delay. I didn't ask enough about what he did with it.”
legacyText.3294995482: Miso sits beneath the chair nearest her. He doesn't look comfortable.
legacyText.3902049271: I keep turning pages. The manual shows two identical sockets facing each other. One is labelled CALL. The other is labelled RECEIVE. In between, a line returns to the caller before the circuit closes.
legacyText.2443307536: “It never asks again. It records the first contact as continuing authority.”
legacyText.234339160: My aunt nods. “When Nadia found out, she tried to shut it down from inside. She thought she could put the original check back.”
legacyText.2156813913: The kettle clicks as it cools. Nobody moves towards it.
legacyText.3024239260: “I got one call,” Leila says. “She said she was handling it. She sounded annoyed with herself. I was annoyed with her too. I told her to stop trying to fix everything alone.”
legacyText.1776811814: “She asked me to stay with you until she got back.”
legacyText.621035776: I look down at the list of declined names. My aunt has made the same mistake as my mother: turning a request into an arrangement that keeps lasting because nobody knows how to end it.
legacyText.2551920913: “I should have told you enough to understand why I didn't have an answer.”
legacyText.434682971: I put the manual down. My hands have started trembling, not dramatically, just enough to make the paper rustle. I hate it. I hold the edge of the table until it stops.
legacyText.2297913303: Imani opens a cupboard, finds mugs and lines four of them beside the kettle. She doesn't ask whether anyone wants tea. The practical interruption gives me somewhere to put my eyes.
legacyText.2940979850: “We need another reader. Independent. Not a replacement body.”
legacyText.2632643031: Miso says, “Adrian still has the original.”
legacyText.3709054161: He lowers his head and scratches at the collar. The brass plate makes a thin sound against his claws.
legacyText.4079219603: “I can tell you where he stores things,” he says. “I can't promise the things are there.”
legacyText.1728055527: Leila turns a page back and points to a smaller diagram I nearly missed. It shows how to release a connection without cutting through it. Two marks, one inside the other, followed by an open end.
legacyText.532577235: “I'm going to teach you this,” she says. “Then you're going to teach it back to me before you try it on anything.”
legacyText.3309256297: I sit down. She gives me a scrap of paper and draws the first line slowly.
legacyText.1023801584: It takes almost an hour. I get impatient twice. She gets impatient once and apologises before I have to point it out. Imani practises with a piece of string. Julian records the sequence in words as well as pictures.
legacyText.2997011219: Miso watches from the chair. When the string loosens without breaking, he looks away.
legacyText.2690776730: I keep the scrap of paper. On the back, under the grocery list already written there, I put the date and the word release.
legacyText.2161845441: Julian finds the box while searching for a spare socket. It sits behind two old lamps in a cupboard my mother told me contained nothing interesting.
legacyText.435633308: Inside are six little clay figures, each about the length of my thumb. They have rough bodies, plain faces and a mark on the back. I take one out. It is surprisingly heavy.
legacyText.3797166827: “Modern practice models,” Julian says. “Nadia made them. Don't start thinking the museum lends out ancient funerary equipment.”
legacyText.3150411103: There are notes under the tissue. Mum has drawn a picture of a worker figure holding a basket, then written several pages about why telling a created thing to perform an endless task is a poor starting point for any safe experiment.
legacyText.3091665949: Her own models are supposed to carry a defined load from one point to another and stop when the task is complete.
legacyText.430711741: I line them up on the table. The figures do not look particularly interested in either description.
legacyText.790233735: Mum's notes describe a way to divide a connection among several temporary holders. It is not enough for the lower station's load. It might be enough to steady a reader while somebody changes a setting.
legacyText.3166857618: Julian gets the second practice handset. I draw the required marks. Imani positions the little figures along the cable, using a ruler because she has decided guessing is how everybody got into trouble.
legacyText.792638836: The first figure moves when I complete the circuit.
legacyText.139509172: Not much. It lifts one foot, puts it down and tips over.
legacyText.4190041479: Julian takes it from her and checks the mark. “The subject's wrong. You're asking it to hold the entire call, not one defined segment.”
legacyText.981267608: I alter the line. This time the figure stands with both feet on the table. The second follows it. Then the third.
legacyText.1683968271: For a few seconds, the handset cable hangs in a precise curve between them without touching the wood.
legacyText.4046058010: I grin before I can help it.
legacyText.1458027392: Then the fourth figure turns towards me.
legacyText.3240180896: “Further instruction?” it asks in my own voice.
legacyText.2372274820: Julian reaches for the circuit. Imani puts one hand above it without touching.
legacyText.209227041: I do. The figure remains standing.
legacyText.2194136585: The fifth figure turns. Then the sixth.
legacyText.2144307414: My drawing has a closed return at the far end. I copied it from an early page in Mum's notes, before the correction on the next sheet. The figures are not ignoring me. The circuit has no recognised completion.
legacyText.353485739: They begin passing the little load back to the first one.
legacyText.372519110: The cable tightens around the ruler. Imani moves her hand away. A crack appears in one clay shoulder.
legacyText.3045096510: I want to snatch the figure up. Julian catches my wrist.
legacyText.3454147860: I take the paper Leila taught me from my pocket. The release sequence is simple enough to remember until I need it. I set it beside the practice mark and copy the first outer line.
legacyText.621201427: The little figures turn with me, all six faces following the chalk.
legacyText.2028721253: “End this task,” I say. “No replacement task. No further holding.”
legacyText.3032017718: One figure sits down. Then another. The cable falls onto the table. The last figure says my name once, quietly, and becomes clay again.
legacyText.1282852514: I pick up the one with the cracked shoulder. Mum's thumbprint is visible near its base. I rub a finger over it and put the figure back in the box.
legacyText.820027003: Julian writes the corrected sequence in large letters. Imani puts a strip of blue tape on the page I missed.
legacyText.4247633241: Leila comes in from the sitting room and looks at the table.
legacyText.3909411330: I could say the figures work. It would be true. I could also omit the part where they nearly broke while following exactly what I asked.
legacyText.225265619: Instead I show her both pages.
legacyText.3377707496: She studies them, then the cracked clay.
legacyText.3791319667: I am ready to defend Mum. Then I remember I was the one standing here when the cable tightened.
legacyText.1815309033: Leila sits down and helps me label every earlier version. She doesn't lecture. She makes me check each page against the next. It takes another half-hour.
legacyText.694562672: At the end, I set three unbroken figures beside a padded tin. They aren't a solution to the whole station. They are a tool for a defined job. I write the exact job on a card and set it beside them.
legacyText.2349455591: Imani reads it before I decide what to carry.
legacyText.1475357042: “Good,” she says. “They get to go home when they're done.”
legacyText.1603237123: Miso lets me examine the collar after everyone else has left the kitchen. That seems important. He waits until Leila is carrying the mugs away, then jumps onto the table and sits with his head turned so the brass plate faces me.
legacyText.2364931899: “What happens if I ask the wrong thing?”
legacyText.2238545281: “Usually I can't answer. Sometimes I can, and regret it.”
legacyText.249007314: I look towards the manual on the table.
legacyText.3673292893: Miso says it flatly. He has stopped doing anything with his tail.
legacyText.127734225: The brass plate is scratched almost smooth. Under the scratches, a name has been pressed into the metal. I can read the first mark, but the rest seem to turn away when I look directly at them.
legacyText.2488291257: “A name I gave him. I was looking for somewhere warm. He had a house with a boiler room. He asked if I would help keep the doors in order.”
legacyText.1846198276: “Ordinary ones, then less ordinary ones. I should have asked better.”
legacyText.1337999824: I wait for a joke. He doesn't provide one.
legacyText.2265996058: “No.” His ears flatten. “She has more important complaints.”
legacyText.3532980640: “A guardian. Small place. Small work. Places collect habits. Some of us learn how to hold them.”
legacyText.1398687967: He looks at the window. A pigeon lands outside, inspects the sill and leaves. His head follows it before he remembers to be upset.
legacyText.2419811604: “Why did you take Mum to him?”
legacyText.1525400594: “I knew she could help with the doors. I didn't know he meant to close one behind her.”
legacyText.4242332662: I want him to say he fought, that he tried to warn her, that he spent eleven months planning to fix it. I don't want a simple statement that leaves me to work out what to feel.
legacyText.2782178980: “Did you try to stop him afterwards?”
legacyText.2091018213: He turns so I can see the bare strip beneath the collar. There are healed scratches on his skin, close together.
legacyText.3287826785: “I need to know where his workshop is,” I say.
legacyText.4142783647: “Then ask me where the equipment was stored when I last saw it. Don't ask where he is now. The wording matters.”
legacyText.2585763114: I ask carefully. He gives me an address near the waterfront, then specifies a side entrance and a set of internal stairs. Julian writes it down from the doorway. Neither of us had heard him return.
legacyText.3087489589: Miso watches the pen move. “Second floor. Room with no windows. There was a yellow cupboard.”
legacyText.3701484017: The collar tightens. I see Miso's shoulders rise before he can stop them.
