legacyText.3853573640: I look at the release diagram. Leila has made me repeat it until I can draw it without looking. The collar is a connection. It carries an agreement. If I can hold both ends and allow a refusal—
legacyText.3109531073: Miso steps back as my hand moves.
legacyText.3281259814: He looks at the chalk. Then at me.
legacyText.263029184: “Not off. Not yet. If it breaks, he knows where I am. Loosen it enough that I can choose where to stand.”
legacyText.54969883: I draw on the table around his paws. The marks need a definite subject. I say his name, Miso, and feel the circle lose its shape.
legacyText.3469767985: “That's what we call you,” I say. “It doesn't work.”
legacyText.129869025: I try again. This time I think about the cat sitting in front of me, the yoghurt lid, the cold fire escape, his decision to come when my door opened. The collar is attached to a name Voss has kept. I am trying to make room for a name its wearer still uses.
legacyText.4193312727: The chalk lifts a fraction from the table.
legacyText.266023740: Miso closes his eyes. He breathes out. The collar loosens enough to leave a narrow gap.
legacyText.3534726044: My hands cramp. Julian puts a glass of water within reach but doesn't touch me. I hold the line for twelve seconds, then twenty. At thirty, Miso steps out of the circle.
legacyText.2581874601: The collar stays on. It is visibly looser.
legacyText.269785599: He sits on the far end of the table, trying to look as if nothing has happened. I drink the water with both hands.
legacyText.723724412: Leila comes back and sees the chalk marks. She begins to speak, then looks at Miso and closes her mouth.
legacyText.1545651169: I clean the table before she can ask. Miso follows the cloth with one paw, a movement so ordinary I almost miss it.
legacyText.1914423853: At the kitchen door he stops.
legacyText.3710432718: “The yellow cupboard has a false back,” he tells Julian. “He changed the lock. Not the wall.”
legacyText.1104839173: Then he goes to sit on my clean school shirt.
legacyText.1882550451: By late afternoon, every map on the table points towards the lake. I begin to suspect maps prefer problems which can be solved by drawing a line downwards.
legacyText.1511783442: Julian marks Voss's workshop, the annex and the old exchange room in different colours. Leila adds places where she has received calls since Nadia disappeared. A hospital car park. A supermarket. The bus stop outside the flat. None is on the line Julian drew.
legacyText.4078045014: She takes the pencil and writes names beside the points. At the hospital car park, Leila had been waiting for a colleague whose husband was dying. At the supermarket she'd met an elderly neighbour who asked after Nadia. At the bus stop, she'd been speaking to me.
legacyText.3256108287: The second set of lines makes an untidy knot.
legacyText.1400450969: Miso stands at the window. “He's getting impatient.”
legacyText.947341554: The glass reflects an extra building on the opposite side of the road. It has too many windows and no ground-floor door. As I watch, a light comes on in each window, one at a time.
legacyText.1056709035: My phone displays nine missed calls. It hasn't rung.
legacyText.2968499276: The first is from Mum. The second is from a schoolfriend I haven't spoken to properly since September. The third has no name. I don't open any of them.
legacyText.3363275915: Julian checks his own screen. The date has changed to Sunday.
legacyText.1242112503: Leila goes to the bell cupboard. She has moved it into the flat inside a locked metal case, because she finally admitted that trying to protect me from a different building was mostly protecting herself from seeing what I was doing. The chalk marks on the case are warmer than the wall around them.
legacyText.3957877527: “We still have time,” she says. “But less room for guessing.”
legacyText.37526656: I look at the copied numbers from Voss's photograph. One is a storage reference. One is an incoming line. The crossed-out one refers to a test Nadia performed before the bypass went in.
legacyText.3833880041: “If we find that recording, we can show what the system was supposed to ask.”
legacyText.721664816: Julian nods. “And use it to calibrate the second reader.”
legacyText.953777992: The reader is in the workshop. The recording is indexed under Eva's name. For the first time, I have a plan with two tasks that can be described without saying something vague about saving everybody.
legacyText.3912540271: Then Dennis phones Leila. I can hear him through the receiver.
legacyText.3528175275: Leila closes her eyes. When she opens them, she is looking at the metal case.
legacyText.1958934196: I start to object. She raises one hand, then lowers it again.
legacyText.3768335327: “I am asking you to hear the plan before arguing. Dennis can hold the case if I show him how. I can stop the annex lines from answering automatically. Then I come to the workshop. I won't enter the other side without telling you.”
legacyText.3213853249: I check the equipment bag. Chalk, manual, notebook, ordinary torch, ordinary first-aid supplies, the feather, water. Imani adds a roll of tape and a screwdriver from her dad's tool bag. She has told him she is helping Leila move storage equipment. He told her to return the screwdriver.
legacyText.1656328144: Julian brings the recorder and a pair of rubber gloves. His injured hand can move at the wrist now, though the fingers remain grey.
legacyText.953676950: On the street, snow has begun to fall. People hunch into their coats. At a crossing, the signal takes so long to change that a man beside me sighs and gives up waiting. He walks to the next corner instead. I watch him go, briefly jealous of a problem with another corner available.
legacyText.1235160484: Imani catches me looking at my phone.
legacyText.475541984: “You can say you're scared without making it the whole plan.”
legacyText.1370103914: At the streetcar stop, an advertisement shows a family laughing around a kitchen table. I have always disliked photographs of families laughing around kitchen tables. Nobody ever looks as if they're laughing at something specific. Now the printed mother turns her head and looks at me.
legacyText.3195248220: The rest of the family keep smiling in the wrong direction.
legacyText.1461143855: Miso presses against my boot. I move between him and the shelter glass.
legacyText.681041411: “You don't have to do that,” he says.
legacyText.2043859782: The printed mother puts a hand against the inside of the advertisement. Her fingers leave marks on the glass.
legacyText.3213047411: Imani takes a step away. “How long until our streetcar?”
legacyText.4230519683: I find Eva's mother's address in a letter attached to the old equipment inventory. The letter asks the archive to stop forwarding calls to her number. It is dated three weeks after Eva died.
legacyText.463299600: Leila reads it without saying anything for a long time.
legacyText.2935570463: “Would it have changed anything?” I ask.
legacyText.420090154: She looks at me. “It should have.”
legacyText.406442544: I go because Julian needs to establish which call was the first, and because the archive record lists Mara Voss as a receiving witness. I do not go because a grieving woman owes me an explanation. I repeat that distinction to myself on the pavement outside her building, trying to make sure it is more than a sentence that lets me knock.
legacyText.2875246504: Imani comes with me. Julian waits in a café across the road with the equipment. Miso has refused to leave the annex's radiator, where he is recovering from the loosened collar.
legacyText.3635795947: Mara answers through the intercom. I give Nadia's name and say there may be a record she can correct. The silence lasts long enough that I start preparing to leave.
legacyText.2128203395: Her flat has plants on the windowsill and a bicycle leaning against the hall wall. It is not arranged around Eva's absence in a way I can read. I am ashamed of having looked for that.
legacyText.1966027465: She lets me stand inside the doorway but does not offer chairs.
legacyText.1263600230: She studies me. There is a family resemblance I didn't notice in the photograph: Eva's eyebrows, the way she held one shoulder slightly higher than the other.
legacyText.905870783: I show her the inventory letter. Mara reads it and hands it back.
legacyText.17572298: I start to explain what the line has become. She holds up one hand.
legacyText.2551710729: Imani gives her the copied witness entry. It is a better choice than offering another story about the dead. Mara checks the date.
legacyText.94391187: She goes to a drawer and brings back a calendar. Not the one Voss kept. This one has appointments, bills, ordinary things continuing after the funeral. She finds a note written between a dentist appointment and a reminder to return a library book.
legacyText.1087109509: “Here. I wrote it down because I thought I was losing my mind.”
legacyText.2152822558: The date is earlier than the archive entry by four days.
legacyText.850736000: Julian's notes come back to me. First contact treated as continuing authority. Reopened channels counted as the same call. Voss changed not just the destination but the point where the record began.
legacyText.1876369055: Mara nods. I write only the date and the source of the correction. When I hand the calendar back, she looks relieved enough that I understand she expected me to ask for the whole page.
legacyText.2468868373: “Did she say anything else?” I ask, then stop. “You don't have to tell us.”
legacyText.2881953066: “She told me where she put a note. That's all I needed.”
legacyText.1650036229: “Adrian wanted another conversation. Then a longer one. Then proof the next voice was her. There was always something else the call needed to do before he could let it end.”
legacyText.3689186971: She doesn't say whether she forgave him. I don't ask.
legacyText.3168958645: “My mum's trapped in his system,” I say.
legacyText.486747525: Mara looks towards the window. On the sill, a plant has grown against the glass and bent back towards the room.
legacyText.17975759: Her attention returns to me at once.
legacyText.1948197069: She closes her eyes. Not in disbelief. As if she has been holding a fact in one place and must now move it without dropping everything around it.
legacyText.400319525: “Tell her I'm sorry I didn't call sooner.”
legacyText.2955844016: “You don't know what I did or didn't do.”
legacyText.744445538: The correction is fair. I had offered her the comfortable sentence because it was easier than hearing another difficult account.
legacyText.2559831904: At the door, Mara asks for Leila's number. I give it only after calling my aunt to ask. The small delay feels awkward. Mara waits without objection.
legacyText.1520204136: Outside, Imani walks half a block before speaking.
legacyText.2090756637: “That she'd helped us, so now she had to help again.”
legacyText.3175701493: Across the road, Julian has ordered one tea and been given a pot large enough for four people. He has spent the waiting time drawing the receiving circuit on a napkin, which the server has tactfully avoided clearing.
legacyText.1326082376: I show him the corrected date. He compares it with the two inventory references, then draws a line beneath the original call.
legacyText.2357244819: “This is the one. Eva's voice, not a later imitation.”
legacyText.3296109676: Imani pours the remaining tea into two cups. It is almost cold. I drink it anyway.
legacyText.133745130: Through the café window, Mara cycles past wearing a bright green helmet. She doesn't see me. She is going somewhere that has nothing to do with my investigation.
legacyText.2880125074: I watch her turn the corner, then look back at the number Julian has circled.
legacyText.4067309688: The recording is not where Julian expects it to be. The index lists Eva Voss under a different surname, the one her mother used. He finds it because I copied the crossed-out number instead of only the replacement.
legacyText.4152585547: In the exchange room, the booth assigned to the original call is full of falling snow.
legacyText.3476039808: Not a picture of snow. Flakes drift against the glass and melt on the floor. Behind them is a kitchen with a yellow blind and a clock shaped like a plate. A telephone lies on the counter, its cord twisted around a chair.
legacyText.1547805106: Voss sits beside it. He looks younger, not because his face has fewer lines but because he hasn't yet learned how to hold it still. A woman stands by the sink. She is wearing a coat over pyjamas.
legacyText.2244254669: Julian nods. “Don't touch either of them. They can't hear us unless we enter the live end.”
legacyText.2695519063: I stand just inside the booth. Snow lands on my sleeve and disappears.
legacyText.2074395391: The phone rings. Voss reaches for it so quickly he knocks the chair over.
legacyText.2719556671: At first there is only static. The woman at the sink takes one step towards him. He lifts a hand to stop her.
legacyText.1179744521: I know how this will end. I know he will hear that voice and spend the next year making other people carry what he cannot put down. Knowing doesn't make it easier to watch him close his eyes.
legacyText.2140796888: The woman puts a hand over her mouth.
legacyText.3990411292: Eva asks about a yellow bowl. I don't understand. Voss does. He says it is still on the shelf. She tells him she put a note underneath it for her mother and forgot to say.
legacyText.2254409776: The woman leaves the kitchen. I hear cupboard doors open in another room. When she comes back she is holding a folded piece of paper. She sits down on the floor beside the sink.
legacyText.529780076: Voss keeps asking questions. Where is Eva? Who is with her? Can she see a door? She answers some and ignores others. Once she asks him to stop talking because she is trying to remember something.
legacyText.736485622: There is a long silence. The snow in the booth falls more slowly.
legacyText.2399147353: “Dad. I don't think that's what it's for.”
legacyText.947463352: He looks towards the control box beside the phone. I recognise the diagram on its lid.
legacyText.2551006499: Voss does not move the receiver from his ear. His wife is still sitting on the floor with the note in her hand. She looks up at him and says his name once.
legacyText.677365159: I find myself standing in the exchange room with snow melting inside my collar.
legacyText.2456651406: “The thing in the flat isn't her.”
legacyText.3172078958: I touch the notebook under my arm. The voice said Mum in my kitchen. It knew her cough, her impatient listen, the way she used my name. Voss had one true call. How many false ones would I have answered to hear mine again?
legacyText.4229641214: Julian copies the acceptance sequence from the booth's control. It isn't a spell that makes a person obey. It records a permission given for one message, with a clear end. When the caller leaves, the receiving side must let the connection close.
legacyText.480538873: Miso sits under the desk, collar almost hidden by his fur.
legacyText.308628791: “You don't get the same person just because you use the same number.”
legacyText.1487033772: I save a transcript of the final exchange in the notebook. Imani asks whether I will show Voss.
legacyText.642881771: She considers that without trying to improve it.
legacyText.115935983: On the booth's inside wall, under the fresh layer of snow, a small handprint appears. Then a second. Someone is pressing against the glass from a place I cannot see.
legacyText.2968684843: A girl's voice speaks from the disconnected phone.
legacyText.4200090900: The voice is lighter than Eva's. The question sounds rehearsed.
legacyText.168334964: Imani steps closer to me. Julian reaches for the booth door, then stops with his good hand just above the handle.
legacyText.311138118: After a while, the voice says, “I haven't got that right yet.”
legacyText.135197998: Voss's workshop occupies the second floor of a narrow commercial building. The tenant downstairs repairs office printers. Someone has left three machines in the corridor with PLEASE COLLECT written on them in increasingly large letters.
legacyText.3159028499: The side entrance is locked. Imani tries the handle once, then steps aside for Julian. He inspects the lock, looks at the screwdriver in her hand and shakes his head.
legacyText.543687406: “What did you think it would be?”
legacyText.1474686918: “I was hoping for a bad one.”
legacyText.3333006543: Miso noses a loose panel beside the stairs. Behind it, a narrow service gap runs up to the next floor. Too small for a person. Large enough for a cat who has several complaints about dust.
legacyText.1647443092: “Don't touch anything yellow until I open the door,” he says.
legacyText.1151016820: Then he disappears into the gap.
legacyText.2632467955: I wait on the stairs. The building hums with ordinary machinery. Below, a printer starts, feeds one sheet of paper and stops. There is an absurd amount of time to think about being arrested. I imagine explaining the bag of chalk and the manual to a police officer. I imagine Leila arriving to collect me and being more disappointed by my poor planning than the offence.
legacyText.3576539082: Miso sits inside the door with a grey cobweb across his face. Imani lifts it off. He pretends to dislike the help while leaning into her hand.
legacyText.3698077003: The workshop is tidy in a way my mother's never was. Drawers are labelled. Cables hang in even loops. On a bench, an open telephone has each removed screw taped beside its original hole.
legacyText.108035450: At the back stands the yellow cupboard.
legacyText.1062671436: Julian checks it against the manual. “Main receiver's in the front. We need the independent reader. Behind.”
legacyText.428323748: Imani goes around the side and finds the thin seam in the false back. She works the screwdriver under it, slowly enough that the wood doesn't split.
legacyText.995912693: On the wall above the bench is a calendar from the year Eva died. The month hasn't been changed. Someone has crossed out the days after her death and stopped halfway through the page.
legacyText.3198151616: A telephone rings in a drawer.
legacyText.2242822202: Imani keeps working. Julian holds the panel steady with his good hand. I press my fingers against the brass feather in my pocket, needing to feel something that doesn't want an answer.
legacyText.79829157: I keep my back to it.
legacyText.1859477746: The panel comes loose. Behind it is a small brass box with two sockets and a sliding lever. Julian lifts it with both hands, forgets about his injured one, and nearly drops it. Imani catches the lower edge.
legacyText.2640379600: The voice in the drawer laughs softly.
legacyText.1513668890: “Not Mum,” I say, mostly to myself.
legacyText.1180242356: The answer is so unexpected that I turn.
legacyText.1018454537: A girl stands beside the open drawer. She has my face, smaller and badly fitted, as if she has remembered the parts without understanding their distances. While I look at her, the features change into Eva's.
legacyText.3339064771: Miso backs against the door. Julian and Imani stand with the reader between them.
legacyText.3402594520: Downstairs, a door closes. I hear shoes on the first flight.
legacyText.1685726277: Imani slides the reader into the equipment bag. “Time to go.”
legacyText.1760702343: The girl moves between me and the exit.
legacyText.1191417017: “You can't take that. He says it makes people leave.”
legacyText.1347101484: The footsteps stop outside the workshop.
legacyText.273548039: Voss tries the handle. It doesn't move. Miso is standing with a paw pressed against a small chalk mark Julian drew beside the hinge.
legacyText.2956279148: “{{firstName}},” Voss calls through the door. “I said you could come and speak to me.”
legacyText.668352135: The girl looks towards him. Her face changes again, into a woman I don't recognise, then an old man with a frightened mouth.
legacyText.3188294044: “You shouldn't have come in here,” she says, in several voices at once.
legacyText.2818273033: Every cable in the room lifts from its hook.
legacyText.123484138: Imani swings the equipment bag over her shoulder and points at the window. I follow her gaze. A flat roof lies three feet below it, across a narrow gap.
legacyText.2668557019: I open the catch. Cold air pours in. The girl reaches for me, stops short of touching my wrist, and looks down at her own hand.
legacyText.1282747566: “Will he make you stay?” she asks.
legacyText.157551296: I look at the tightening cables. At Miso holding the door. At the spare key hanging beside the light switch where he could never have reached it without climbing into the claim.
legacyText.3735296334: The girl stares at me. Behind the door, Voss says a name I can't hear clearly.
legacyText.2463677099: Imani goes through the window first. She drops onto the roof, turns and holds out both hands for the equipment bag. Julian passes it down, then climbs after it with his injured hand tucked against his chest.
legacyText.2037589043: Miso is still at the door.
legacyText.3028549085: The cables have reached the floor. One moves over my boot with the deliberate pressure of a finger testing fabric. I lift my foot. It follows.
legacyText.422698921: I take the chalk from my pocket and draw the first release mark on the desk. The line breaks where the surface is covered in varnish. I rub it away and try on the exposed wood beneath a scratch.
legacyText.702269969: The girl's face changes as she watches.
legacyText.2140774672: Miso makes another small sound. I don't look at him. If I look at him, I'll hurry the last line and lose it.
legacyText.226681199: “Can you hold this end?” I ask the girl.
legacyText.2529720600: “Not for him,” I say. “For the cat. Only until he moves. Then you stop.”
legacyText.2724157569: She looks at the mark, then at her own hands. The cables around my boots loosen.
legacyText.1188495678: She puts two fingers inside the outer circle. The chalk glows a dull white. I feel a resistance at the edge of the mark, something trying to keep its old shape.
legacyText.4110185196: Miso lifts his paw from the door.
legacyText.1354438689: The handle turns. I scoop him up, feel his claws close hard around my sleeve, and run for the window.
legacyText.2133126889: Voss opens the door behind me.
legacyText.1424929298: The girl pulls her hand out of the chalk circle. I am already on the sill. She looks towards him, then towards the gap.
legacyText.1294156470: I don't tell her what to do. I drop.
legacyText.3891426629: The roof knocks the air out of my chest. Imani catches my coat, preventing me from sliding into a shallow pool beside the gutter. Miso scrambles out of my arms and crouches against a vent.
legacyText.36947179: Above me, Voss leans out of the window.
legacyText.3503319573: “That isn't going to hold the line by itself,” he calls. “You need the calibration I gave Nadia.”
legacyText.3997844919: Julian is checking the brass reader. “We have it.”
legacyText.3815848520: “No,” Voss says, and for the first time he sounds genuinely alarmed. “You have the original. The load changed.”
legacyText.3236865926: The girl steps onto the sill beside him.
legacyText.3366321624: She looks at the snow collecting on the roof.
legacyText.3809471439: She lowers herself over the edge. For a moment her shape stretches too far, hand still on the sill while her feet touch the roof. Then she lets go and stands beside me, small and barefoot.
legacyText.2371428942: Voss says her borrowed name again. She covers her ears.
legacyText.860094432: The roof door is locked from the other side. Imani goes at it with the screwdriver. Julian holds the bag. I keep my body between the girl and the window, although I'm not sure either of us would survive Voss deciding to pull a connection instead of calling.
legacyText.2373208119: Then Leila opens the roof door.
legacyText.3975243425: All of us stare at her.
legacyText.3878203164: She has Dennis behind her. He looks at the workshop window, the girl and the equipment bag, then decides not to ask until everyone is inside.
legacyText.2915862055: Downstairs, the printer-repair tenant is standing by his front door with folded arms.
legacyText.6204499: “Do I need to call the police?”
legacyText.3069271469: “Yes,” Leila says. “Tell them there's an electrical hazard upstairs. Stay out until someone checks it.”
legacyText.1071736119: She doesn't try to give him the rest. I am learning that honesty can be a matter of answering the question someone actually needs answered.
legacyText.325557424: On the street, the girl stops under a lamp. Snow passes through her shoulder, then begins to settle. She holds one flake on the back of her hand and watches it melt.
legacyText.1784433032: Miso approaches her slowly. His collar is twisted to one side. She crouches and offers him her empty hand. He sniffs it without touching.
legacyText.3403992520: “What do I call you?” I ask.
legacyText.1542423277: The girl looks across the road. On the pavement near a hedge, a small brown bird hops away from the lights.
legacyText.904296639: The girl considers both names with obvious seriousness.
legacyText.4233336506: Her face changes. Eva's features loosen. For a moment she looks unfinished, a person drawn before the lines have been rubbed clean. Then she settles into a face I have never seen before.
legacyText.2175984806: Dennis opens the car door. “Can she wear a seat belt?”
legacyText.2353459050: Wren looks at it, then at me.
legacyText.4100184953: In the back seat, Imani passes her a spare pair of gloves. Wren puts both on the same hand, studies the result and waits for someone to explain.
legacyText.1056143357: Nobody laughs. Imani takes one off and shows her how.
legacyText.1928344446: Wren spends the drive watching the windscreen wipers. Each time they move she leans forward slightly, as if expecting them to take part of the view away.
legacyText.3516694465: He points to the guttering at the edge of the windscreen. She follows the movement all the way down and nods to herself.
legacyText.2118139541: At the annex, Leila clears a space in the storeroom. She does not put Wren inside a chalk circle. She tells everyone this before someone can suggest it.
legacyText.2131860343: Wren stands by the doorway, looking at the salt marks around the bell case.
legacyText.3097664195: “They're for the connection,” Leila says. “We'll keep them away from you.”
legacyText.1596016194: “Then I'll be more specific. You can sit by the radiator. Nobody will close a mark around you without asking. If we think there's a danger, we'll tell you before doing anything.”
legacyText.2614538505: Wren sits on the floor beside the radiator. Miso stays near the opposite wall. They watch each other with matching suspicion.
legacyText.944475574: Julian puts the second reader on the table. He wants to test it immediately. I want to ask Wren about Mum. Imani goes to the vending machine and comes back with plain crackers because nobody knows whether Wren can eat.
legacyText.4078444935: She can hold one. She turns it over several times.
legacyText.3181274863: “I don't usually plan that far with a cracker.”
legacyText.1450499221: Wren looks at her. Then she smiles, briefly and uncertainly. It is the first expression I've seen on her face that doesn't seem borrowed.
legacyText.166494731: When she bites the cracker, half of it falls into her lap. She stares at the crumbs, annoyed.
legacyText.4135375393: I sit on the floor a little way from her.
legacyText.3237336219: Wren puts the remaining cracker down.
legacyText.2699491254: I have to breathe before asking the next question.
legacyText.1828854169: “Did you know what would happen to Julian?”
legacyText.1478593926: She looks at his bandaged hand. “I know now.”
legacyText.3988418725: Julian doesn't say it's all right. He sets down the wire he is holding and turns towards her.
legacyText.954873376: “I don't want him to put me back.”
legacyText.3895512204: The room is quiet enough for me to hear the vending machine compressor start in the corridor.
legacyText.1773514129: I ask what happens when the Exchange opens fully. Wren rubs a crumb between her fingers until it disappears.
legacyText.2640869409: “All the voices come through. Dad says we can find the right one.”
legacyText.2735616845: “Voss,” I say, then regret correcting her so sharply.
legacyText.4095004965: She presses her hands against the sides of her head. “A lot. Some are small. Some are shouting. Some don't know they're finished.”
legacyText.2444018842: “Sometimes. If I use a face they like. Then they listen.”
legacyText.4193517780: I think of my own face outside the flat. The note under the glass.
legacyText.4057368713: “Your mother said it when she was tired. Your name. I heard it so much I thought it was somewhere.”
legacyText.1834415033: “A place she was trying to go.”
legacyText.1353689816: I look away. Imani moves the cracker packet a little closer to Wren, although she hasn't asked for another.
legacyText.602901659: Julian asks about the changing load. Wren is better at explaining that than at explaining herself. The messages have been accumulating because Voss keeps the receiving lines open. Every unanswered call borrows capacity from the next. Nadia has been holding the group apart with one manual control. By dawn, there will be too many connections for her to distinguish.
legacyText.491975797: “The second reader can ask each one whether it wants to go,” Julian says.
legacyText.1348428377: “It can ask,” Wren says. “It doesn't know who's answering.”
legacyText.2723641016: She watches me for a long time.
legacyText.3765475927: She picks the cracker up again. “You ask and then you do the other thing. You say if, and then I have to.”
legacyText.2412361077: Leila sits down beside the table. She does it slowly, with her hands visible on her knees.
legacyText.1660631431: “We need to work out what happens to you if the messages leave,” she says. “We can't pretend we already know.”
legacyText.740847684: Wren looks at her. The radiator clicks behind her shoulder.
legacyText.2002047337: I cannot promise she won't. The temptation is so strong it makes my mouth feel full of words I shouldn't use.
legacyText.2029847981: Instead I ask, “Can we find out before we decide?”
legacyText.3889706029: Wren draws one knee up. The glove on her left hand has begun to slip through her fingers. She pushes it back into place.
legacyText.708730795: I sit with her while Julian begins testing the reader. For a while nobody asks Wren to do anything useful.
legacyText.2921896897: “Just keep up,” Imani repeats from the alley. “That was the first thing you asked of me. I noticed.”
legacyText.178717979: The reader works on a piece of string. It works on a paper connection. It works on an empty telephone circuit Julian builds from two handsets and a coil of cable Dennis finds in a cupboard.
legacyText.3945100960: It fails when Wren puts one finger against the brass socket.
legacyText.2695975847: Every light in the storeroom goes out. Leila holds the bell case shut while Julian pulls the contact free. In the sudden dark, somebody knocks a glass off the table. I hear it break near my feet.
legacyText.3890071181: The emergency lights come on. Wren is standing by the door. The borrowed gloves lie empty on the floor.
legacyText.1098064025: Julian looks at the reader's indicator. It has counted three thousand four hundred and eleven responses in less than a second.
legacyText.1604523044: Wren backs out of the room.
legacyText.3184631023: I follow her into the corridor before anyone can stop me. She is pressed against the wall beside the vending machine, looking down at her hands.
legacyText.2692171210: “I said I didn't know,” she says.
legacyText.3151183971: I don't know what my face is doing. I make myself look at the machine instead. Someone has put a packet of crisps in the wrong spiral, and two flavours are wedged together behind the glass.
legacyText.4223841280: “I thought we had it,” I say.
legacyText.1707240010: The sentence stings because I can hear the possible truth in it. I had started thinking of Wren as the missing part of the circuit. Not the person who couldn't work out a pair of gloves.
legacyText.3616816515: Imani comes out with a dustpan. She sets it against the wall and stands between us, leaving room for Wren to move away.
legacyText.3793914994: “We're going to need a different way to count,” she says.
legacyText.1405499673: Julian appears in the doorway. “We don't have time to rebuild a whole—”
legacyText.1811727079: “Then don't start by telling her she's impossible.”
legacyText.2178278208: Leila joins me a minute later. Her palm is red where the case burned through the cloth. She has wrapped it in a damp towel.
legacyText.2713274255: “We need the original receiving record,” she says. “The part that establishes who is answering. There should be one for every person the line can name.”
legacyText.2296353491: “Then we ask how to make one.”
legacyText.2438143092: He knows the answer before my aunt gives it. His face changes.
legacyText.787422979: “No. The last time I asked somebody down there to fix a record, they took a year of my life I can describe but can't remember.”
legacyText.1667095076: “Then we don't give them an undefined payment,” Leila says.
legacyText.3278046000: “You make it sound like I forgot to read a form.”
legacyText.1366635957: My aunt goes quiet. The correction lands hard enough that I see her accept it before she answers.
legacyText.3803312696: For a while nobody has a useful next sentence.
legacyText.1020617455: Imani takes me into the empty stairwell. I think she wants help moving something, until she closes the fire door behind me.
legacyText.288981609: I lean against the handrail. It is cold through the sleeve of my coat.
legacyText.2602607100: I tell her what Julian said about the messages entering one person. I tell her how simple it seemed, for a second, to stand where Mum was standing. She doesn't interrupt. When I've finished, she sits down on a stair.
legacyText.2721585174: “And everyone else carries on deciding how to fix things, except now there's another person stuck.”
legacyText.3917160092: I sit on the step above her. From the storeroom comes the muffled sound of Leila and Julian moving the table.
legacyText.2401893652: Imani looks up at me. “You told me Voss hadn't contacted you. I remember asking. I walked into his workshop thinking you had the same information I did.”
legacyText.4118103623: “That wasn't yours to fix by lying.”
legacyText.3661242500: I start to explain about the photograph and stop when I hear myself arranging the facts into something easier to excuse. She waits. Eventually I say, “I wanted you there. I should have asked.”
legacyText.2697390166: Imani rubs a mark on the stair with the edge of her glove. “You told me when Voss contacted you. That's why I'm still here. I can deal with a bad plan if I'm actually allowed to know it's bad.”
legacyText.670942608: “I haven't told you every thought I've had.”
legacyText.2010090267: “I don't need every thought. I need the bit that puts me on a roof with someone else's cables chasing my feet.”
legacyText.2766308006: She takes a deep breath. “I can be your friend without agreeing to everything.”
legacyText.1331868734: I look at her. She seems annoyed at having to say friend out loud. I am grateful enough to keep my own face turned towards the rail.
legacyText.828123572: She studies me for a moment, then gets up. I pick the dustpan up on the way back. There is still broken glass in the room, and somebody needs to clear it before the next emergency.
legacyText.3284799: Wren moves to Imani’s other side when I reach for the door. The broken torch is still in my bag.
legacyText.307357508: Wren keeps her receiving card turned away from me. “You said he gave you permission. I remember.”
legacyText.3501017090: Anubis meets me at the bottom of the concrete staircase. He is carrying the driver's cap under one arm. Without it, he looks taller.
legacyText.1137251804: Miso stops two steps above him.
legacyText.2367621288: “We need a receiving record,” I say.
legacyText.3001900634: “Someone who does not enjoy being called from a laundry basement.”
legacyText.682760684: I think of the three pens and decide not to ask whether gods complain about each other in a group chat.
legacyText.938641805: Leila has stayed at the annex with Dennis and the bell. Julian came as far as the staircase and stopped. I found him standing with his good hand on the rail, looking at the place where the concrete becomes stone.
legacyText.1700657469: I told him where I was going and when I would return. He checked the time himself. Neither of us called it cowardice.
legacyText.3118851437: Now I follow Anubis down a corridor lined with doors. Behind one, someone is grinding grain. Behind another, a woman and a man argue over the ownership of a boat. Nothing resembles the endless fire I expected from the word underworld when I first heard it in a classroom.
legacyText.1836822694: At the far end is an office with two chairs. A scale stands against the wall. It is small and practical, its pans scratched from use.
legacyText.3439684226: “This isn't the judgment of the dead. Nobody is weighing your heart. Sit down.”
legacyText.2245615341: I do. Imani remains standing. Wren stays beside the door with her hands in the pockets of the coat Leila found for her. The sleeves reach past her fingers.
legacyText.1270964792: A woman enters from the other room. She wears a plain white dress with a narrow blue border. There is a feather on the desk beside her, its shaft worn smooth by handling.
legacyText.2606705484: “You have brought a person whose record is attached to several thousand senders,” she says.
legacyText.2759156656: “Do you want that record separated?” the woman asks her.
legacyText.2508328976: Wren looks at me. I make myself remain silent.
legacyText.890229272: “I want to know what happens after.”
legacyText.509172374: “Good. Then that is the first question.”
legacyText.68559883: The woman places three blank cards on the desk. On one she writes sender. On one, message. On the third, receiver. She puts a pebble on each.
legacyText.319935640: “When the circuit operates as intended, these remain distinguishable. The message passes. The sender can leave. The receiver can refuse.”
legacyText.1147578809: “Someone has made refusal count as continued attendance. Over time the messages have begun using one another to remain legible.”
legacyText.2768779038: “Is the person who has grown in those connections. That doesn't mean she owns everyone she can hear.”
legacyText.690634727: Wren's hands come out of the coat pockets.
legacyText.46644890: I hear Mum's recording in my head. The room, the second reader, the problem of recognising who is actually answering.
legacyText.3465550899: The woman turns the third card over. On its back is an empty box.
legacyText.3478975830: “A receiving record establishes a person independently of what they carry. But it requires the person to claim it. It cannot be issued to Voss's daughter on behalf of somebody who isn't Voss's daughter.”
legacyText.3119533616: “He says names have to be old.”
legacyText.1670346284: “People say many convenient things about names.”
legacyText.3953612647: Anubis stands at the wall, giving nobody help they haven't asked for. I want him to tell me what to do. I suspect he knows this.
legacyText.2684748446: The woman holds out the blank card to Wren.
legacyText.3107051371: “What name do you ask us to record?”
legacyText.3301681422: She looks at me again. Then at Imani, who has been waiting quietly beside her.
legacyText.3389996722: The woman writes the name. The pebble on the third card separates from the others.
legacyText.3212943100: Wren gasps. For one second her face becomes empty, too smooth to read. Imani takes a step towards her and stops before touching.
legacyText.164824653: Wren nods. Imani takes her hand.
legacyText.817853883: The features return slowly. I recognise the face she chose under the streetlight. Her mouth trembles with effort.
legacyText.3079313923: “There are still too many,” she says.
legacyText.3779347428: “The record gives you somewhere to stand,” the woman says. “It doesn't remove the people holding the road closed.”
legacyText.3899369271: She hands me a copy of the receiving sequence, but gives Wren the original card. I don't reach for it. Wren presses it against her chest as if she has only just found out where to keep something important.
legacyText.3301177681: On the way out, I ask Anubis whether the woman was Ma'at.
legacyText.3785828161: He looks at me for a while.
legacyText.3514579355: “You met someone doing the work of her office. It may be enough to remember the work.”
legacyText.4194586739: At the staircase, Julian is still there. He has brought the trolley up from the landing because he couldn't stand waiting without doing anything.
legacyText.786683651: He looks at it and then at her. Very carefully, he says, “Hello, Wren.”
legacyText.1832518893: She grins. It changes her whole face.
legacyText.1889513399: The road back from the witness office passes a doorway which wasn't there when I arrived. Beyond it lie fields under a sky too bright for midnight. Water moves along narrow channels. Someone is repairing a wooden gate, swearing at a peg which refuses to fit.
legacyText.3574605025: Anubis looks through the opening. “People. Different matter.”
legacyText.605184645: A woman carrying a basket comes towards the road. She sets it down beside the gate and helps the man hold the wood level. Neither looks particularly interested in me.
legacyText.3708844628: I had expected the dead to be waiting. Here they are busy.
legacyText.1518136503: “One way of describing a desired place,” Anubis says. “People make places by living in them too.”
legacyText.634178758: Imani watches the man try the peg again. “Does he want a hammer?”
legacyText.3312893411: “He wants the peg he made to fit.”
legacyText.694601997: The answer sounds sufficiently ordinary that she smiles.
legacyText.628300744: Wren takes one step through the doorway. I start to reach for her, then stop. She has a receiving record now. She is not a lost cable that must be kept within reach.
legacyText.1387683055: “For a little while. Don't mistake being welcomed for being expected to remain.”
legacyText.2797328248: The ground under my boots is warm. After two days of snow and radiators which never quite heat the room, the sensation is so unexpected that I almost sit down.
legacyText.104371535: The woman beside the gate glances at me.
legacyText.2392829409: “Mind the irrigation channel. Looks shallower than it is.”
legacyText.2776722008: Then she returns to the gate.
legacyText.285744949: Wren kneels beside the water. Her reflection appears slowly, the chosen face settling into the moving surface. She looks over her shoulder at Imani.
legacyText.47905095: Imani crouches beside her. Their reflections meet in the water. For a while they stay like that without turning it into a lesson.
legacyText.3856694938: I walk to the edge of the field with Anubis. The plants are tall enough to move against my sleeves. Farther away, a group of people are carrying baskets towards a house. One pauses to adjust a sandal, falls behind, then hurries to catch the others.
legacyText.2944196228: Anubis looks out over the field.
legacyText.1082088056: “That isn't information I owe every person who asks.”
legacyText.2882549741: I let the question go. It is more difficult because he hasn't made it sound foolish.
legacyText.1785027939: Near the gate, the peg finally slides into place. The man steps back and tests the wood with both hands. The woman picks up her basket. A task finishes. Nobody asks what must immediately replace it.
legacyText.300468046: Wren comes to stand beside me.
legacyText.2244038384: “If I let the voices leave, do I get a place like this?”
legacyText.4290035667: Anubis kneels so he is closer to her height.
legacyText.1667278595: “You may need to find out what you want after you can hear yourself think.”
legacyText.3603541479: She considers this with obvious dissatisfaction. It is a relief to see her dislike an answer without changing her face to please the person giving it.
legacyText.2713593648: Julian waits at the road. He has stayed on the threshold, not because anyone stopped him but because he has discovered a limit he intends to keep. I go back to him before he has to call my name.
legacyText.4271442948: I understand what she means. The waiting messages have made the dead seem like a single enormous need. Seeing someone argue with a gate puts them back into separate lives. I am not trying to satisfy an ocean of grief. I am trying to stop a machine from making one person's absence into everybody else's obligation.
legacyText.638821517: Wren takes the receiving card out of her pocket. She holds it by the edges, away from the water.
legacyText.1206622795: “I want to stay with my own name,” she tells Julian.
legacyText.3631700517: He nods. “Then we'll set the reader to recognise the record before it accepts the messages.”
legacyText.778313807: She puts the card away. The man at the gate has started walking towards the house, carrying the unused pegs in one hand. He doesn't look back.
legacyText.522833177: At the doorway, I notice a figure sitting in the shade, sewing a tear in a coat. For a second my chest tightens. The angle of the head is familiar. The way the person holds the fabric between two fingers.
legacyText.100179586: Then they look up. Not Mum. A stranger, mildly annoyed by being stared at.
legacyText.2271853836: Outside, the night returns. My boots are cold again. Imani checks the time and sends her dad a message before putting her phone away.
legacyText.2446654118: I ask Anubis whether he will come with me.
legacyText.1319013241: I nod before he has to explain the passengers, the road, the jobs which do not stop because I found a worse one. He looks almost relieved.
legacyText.1590672274: At the top of the stair, Miso waits beside Julian's trolley. He sees Wren holding the new card and sniffs the edge.
legacyText.2473684351: She smiles. The reflection in the stairwell window smiles with her.
legacyText.1821204936: Voss is waiting outside the annex when I return. He stands under the security light with his hands visible and his phone on the pavement beside him.
legacyText.4049126101: Dennis has locked the gate. Leila stands inside it with the metal case at her feet.
legacyText.2463537841: “I didn't let him in,” she says.
legacyText.2670023417: Voss looks at Wren. For a moment he seems unable to place her. Then his eyes find the borrowed coat.
legacyText.2934742571: He looks at me. “What have you done?”
legacyText.4149742572: “Three thousand four hundred and eleven responses,” Julian says. “At least. Your load count was wrong.”
legacyText.275415330: Voss turns towards him. The courtesy drains away.
legacyText.2685739983: “That's an instantaneous count. Not an accumulation. Some will be duplicates.”
legacyText.2318314672: He looks back at the gate. Leila doesn't move.
legacyText.2432699253: For a while the two engineers argue through the bars. Voss is better informed about the current load. Julian has the original calibration. Neither has enough on his own, and both know it. I listen until their sentences become so specific that the fear underneath them almost disappears.
legacyText.339463798: Leila picks up his phone with a cloth and passes it through the gate.
legacyText.85492483: “We need information you have. That's different from giving you control.”
legacyText.2501666538: He takes the phone. His hand shakes once before he closes it around the case.
legacyText.230548123: I show him the transcript of Eva's first call.
legacyText.1378280882: He reads the first line and stops.
legacyText.2834607674: “Then you know she said she had to go.”
legacyText.4167830748: “Did you ever find the note under the bowl?”
legacyText.164556253: He looks at me as if I have touched him without permission.
legacyText.3643987957: I put the transcript away. I hadn't meant to give him that answer. It leaves us both with the strange discomfort of an argument that doesn't finish in the expected place.
legacyText.465215715: Wren comes to the gate. She stands where Voss can see her face clearly.
legacyText.2753480359: “I remember the calls,” she says. “I don't remember the kitchen. I know the words because you kept playing them.”
legacyText.2231554036: Voss puts one hand on the bars. “You don't have to remember everything at once.”
legacyText.2919358528: Behind him, a bus goes past with most of its seats empty. The driver waits at the red light even though there is no traffic. I find myself staring at the patient, ordinary obedience of it.
legacyText.874363759: Leila opens the gate only far enough to put a chair outside.
legacyText.4044983629: “If you give us the revised load sequence, we'll record your contribution. Nobody will pretend you didn't help. You won't operate the reader.”
legacyText.1166920343: “The thing inside won't let you close the line.”
legacyText.362498469: Wren steps back from the gate.
legacyText.1150417495: I see her face begin to change, and realise she is trying to find one he will listen to. I put my notebook down before my hands can become part of another instruction.
legacyText.1078021716: “Wren,” I say, quietly. “You don't have to.”
legacyText.3368596139: She looks at me. The face settles.
legacyText.1955456897: Voss sits in the chair. For the next twenty minutes he dictates numbers to Julian. He stops twice to correct a figure and once to insist that a particular connection must remain open. Julian writes the correction down and refuses the open connection.
legacyText.3022675039: When the sequence is finished, Leila checks it against the original.
legacyText.1088358405: He looks towards Wren, who is sitting on the inside step with Miso beside her.
legacyText.2335952632: I read the new figure. Four minutes to hold the broken connections, ask the questions the bypass removed, release my mother and bring everybody through. After two days of searching, the answer fits inside a number I can count on one hand.
legacyText.233824889: “I can hold the master line. From inside.”
legacyText.1320206309: Leila looks at me. This time she doesn't decide in advance which answer I am allowed to hear.
legacyText.536026900: I look at Voss's hands. No cable burns. No grey skin. He has found ways to stay outside the machinery he built.
legacyText.1551618545: “If you come,” I say, “you don't get a private channel.”
legacyText.29847962: “And if Wren says no, she means no.”
legacyText.2682897470: He looks as if he might argue about the name again. Then he picks his phone up from the chair and puts it in his pocket.
legacyText.4021300514: I do not mistake the words for a guarantee. Julian writes them down anyway.
legacyText.1676664592: Julian looks at the spare connector, then at his bandaged hand. “Tell me before you choose a piece of equipment over the person holding it.”
legacyText.2851385728: Julian checks the reader, then meets my eyes. “You pulled me out. I can hold this end.”
legacyText.2587528139: Nobody likes rehearsing an emergency. Leila says this while making everyone do it a third time.
legacyText.1083494014: Julian has arranged the equipment on two tables. The bell case is at one end, the second reader at the other. Between them lie paper cards representing Nadia, the waiting messages, Wren, the witness, and the operator. He has drawn a little cat on the card for Miso. Miso has been trying to sit on it ever since.
legacyText.125039128: “You're not a load-bearing component,” Julian tells him.
legacyText.3490502082: Voss stands near the door. Dennis watches him from a chair, holding a mug with both hands. There is no realistic reason a retired security officer with a mug should intimidate Voss. It appears to be working anyway.
legacyText.4212825603: The first rehearsal fails because I close the holding mark before Imani positions the reader. The second fails because Julian changes a setting with the wrong hand and knocks the lever out of alignment. The third fails because Wren says she isn't ready and everyone else takes too long to stop.
legacyText.1307649271: “We stop when she says it,” I say.
legacyText.732429483: “If we stop at the wrong time—”
legacyText.523787789: “Then we need to know what stopping means before we're in there.”
legacyText.3330228237: I hear Leila's teaching voice in my own. It is irritating and useful.
legacyText.463254016: Julian marks three stages on the table with tape. Before the first, I can withdraw. Between the first and second, the system holds temporarily. After the second, the messages have begun to separate; stopping then means choosing another way to contain them.
legacyText.1005290774: “Break the bell,” Leila says. “Sever the crossing. It will get us out, but unfinished messages will lose the only route we know how to reach.”
legacyText.52320890: Wren looks at her card. Her name is written in Julian's cramped hand beside the words independent receiving record.
legacyText.4191271759: “The record should keep you separate,” Julian says. “I can't promise what the shock will do.”
legacyText.1096845656: I appreciate the honest sentence and hate the uncertainty inside it.
legacyText.1757319270: Voss takes a pen and points to the operator's card. “There is one further option. A live receiver could hold the load while the rest of you disconnect. With the bypass removed, it would no longer be forced.”
legacyText.736512603: Mum held it for eleven months. I think about how Voss has arranged the possibility so it sounds newly reasonable now that he has said willing.
legacyText.665963898: Julian puts a second card underneath the operator.
legacyText.861977379: “One person. No ordinary way out. We'd have to build a new receiving point from outside.”
legacyText.2546242540: “We don't choose that by accident,” Imani says.
legacyText.1676081166: We rehearse again. This time Wren says stop halfway through, and all of us stop. Miso takes his paw off the cat card. Julian lowers the lever. Imani sets the reader down. I open the outer line of the mark without breaking the inner one.
legacyText.2921206898: Nothing falls. Nothing is trapped. Wren breathes out and looks almost embarrassed by her relief.
legacyText.2776979165: We go again. At the end, Julian checks the timer.
legacyText.2867996614: Imani looks at the table. “Thirty-two spare.”
legacyText.4284525672: Voss does not look at him.
legacyText.1681484771: Leila packs the equipment. She labels everything in large letters, including the bag containing chalk, which nobody was likely to confuse with anything else. I do not tease her. I have started to understand how much fear can fit inside being organised.
legacyText.138858425: Miso noses the edge of my notebook. A page I haven't read falls open. On it, Mum has sketched several jackal figures in different poses. Beneath one she has written Wepwawet, Opener of the Ways. Beside the name is a note: Ask for a road, not ownership of the road. Courtesy isn't payment. Precision matters.
legacyText.1704252277: I read the name aloud carefully. Miso looks towards the door.
legacyText.1593128514: “He may be there,” he says. “When the lower route narrows.”
legacyText.1034165664: “Knowing which name to use helps. Don't assume any name gives you command.”
legacyText.3636915269: I mark the page with a strip of blue tape. Imani does the same to the release diagram, then hands the roll back without saying anything about whether she trusts me to remember it.
legacyText.1872196632: Near midnight, Dennis brings the car around. Leila checks every latch on the bell case. Voss carries the equipment bag under Imani's supervision. Julian signs the archive's paper register before leaving, including an estimated return time.
legacyText.4043127037: I look at the blank line after his signature.
legacyText.1568715121: I write my name under his. My ordinary name, in my ordinary handwriting, with a pen that is running out of ink. Then I close the register and follow the others out.
legacyText.3125757631: The guardian’s gaze stops on the marks of my earlier forced crossing. Knowing a name will not make him overlook how I treated the last road. I will need another way to ask.
legacyText.1129556226: The lower entrance is inside a disused service building near the waterfront. The building is Voss's invention before it is a place: temporary walls, false measurements, a real electricity supply someone has continued paying for. From the pavement it looks like something waiting to be demolished.
legacyText.845314603: Leila has brought Dennis to hold the outer line. He checks the chair she sets beside the bell case, tests its legs and sits down.
legacyText.4022609987: “Then tell me when you connect the reader.”
legacyText.1098630670: She promises. He takes a small battery timer from his pocket. I am glad someone in the room still believes a timer can do its job without developing a second meaning.
legacyText.2369745629: Voss opens the inner door with a key. It leads to a staircase which should come out below ground. Instead it descends beside a wall of dark water. A fish passes on the other side, turns, and is gone.
legacyText.3118274991: Imani puts her hand on the rail.
legacyText.1511248061: “It will hold while the outer line remains stable.”
legacyText.3287250367: We go down in single file. Miso moves ahead, stopping at every landing to sniff the corner. Wren stays near the back with Julian. She keeps looking at the water and then touching the card in her pocket.
legacyText.2021444178: Halfway down, the lights go out behind me.
legacyText.2893025368: Nobody speaks. I take out the torch and point it at the steps. The beam catches water running upward along a crack in the concrete. Something knocks against the wall on the other side, three slow impacts.
legacyText.2260432336: My body knows the rhythm before I do.
legacyText.3834729328: The corridor at the bottom ends in a pair of stone doors. A narrow opening lies between them. Through it, I can see the lights of the lower station and, far above those lights, the upside-down shape of Toronto.
legacyText.3583523365: Between me and the opening stands a figure carrying a standard topped by a jackal.
legacyText.4039788768: He doesn't look like Anubis. Even before I can decide why, the distinction feels important. His posture is forward, alert, the way a person stands before a race begins. When he turns towards me, the end of the standard scrapes a line through the dust.
legacyText.226184061: Voss steps forward. “The operator is expecting us.”
legacyText.2142096105: The standard comes down between him and the doors.
legacyText.3417359232: I find the page in Mum's notebook. The sketch is rough, but the shape of the standard is unmistakable.
legacyText.3401503066: Wepwawet looks at the open book.
legacyText.1560204665: “The conservator,” he says. “She asked better questions after the first one.”
legacyText.760033539: “What was the first one?” I ask.
legacyText.738809420: “How to get in without being stopped.”
legacyText.3271349212: I hear Julian draw a breath behind me. Wren moves closer to the wall. The pressure of the waiting voices has changed her shape at the edges; her sleeves look too long even for the borrowed coat.
legacyText.3537220329: Wepwawet examines each of us. When he reaches Miso, his eyes stop at the collar.
legacyText.3745298216: “A useful distinction. Not yet a release.”
legacyText.2424744122: I think of the circle on the kitchen table. I loosened the collar but didn't remove it. Voss has been quiet for too long.
legacyText.3808721971: “He knows the route. If he runs—”
legacyText.1976338651: The stone doors shift. The gap narrows by an inch.
legacyText.3339882819: Voss looks at the standard, then at the cat. He says a word I don't recognise. Miso folds to the floor as the collar loosens completely.
legacyText.3500650061: I kneel beside him. He is breathing. His eyes stay open, fixed on Voss.
legacyText.3635718434: “You don't have to come farther,” I say.
legacyText.3077171410: He gets up slowly. Walks to the edge of the dust line. Looks through the doors.
legacyText.2198117042: He crosses back and stands beside my boot.
legacyText.510631254: I could offer the witness receipt and negotiate passage for every person who wants it. I could invoke the office-name I learned, asking him to open a road without claiming it as mine. I could try to force the doors while they are still apart, though the standard hasn't moved an inch and the water beside me is rising.
legacyText.3870930145: Or I could turn back. The upper route remains open. There would still be time to cut the outer bell, but not to reach Nadia first.
legacyText.3102076067: I put the torch down so both hands are visible.
legacyText.664668369: My knee will not take my full weight. Imani carries the reader while I use the wall. Forcing the earlier crossing has not stayed behind at the doors.
legacyText.684867585: Beyond the doors, the lower station opens around me. It is larger than it was during the first rescue, or I am arriving from a side I didn't see. Rows of switchboards rise towards an arch of dark water. Telephone cables hang between stone columns. Every cable carries a brass label.
legacyText.4172756414: Some are written in letters I recognise. Some use scripts I cannot read. A few are only marks, as if the person writing them had almost forgotten the shape before reaching the end.
legacyText.1973946174: Julian stops beside one, not touching it.
legacyText.2979373294: “Those aren't all dead callers,” he says.
legacyText.2003095416: Leila looks at the label. She recognises the name.
legacyText.1879697103: “It's a patient. From the first tests. She declined.”
legacyText.2218556507: I turn towards him. “You kept them.”
legacyText.2571647485: “I kept the routing information. I didn't send—”
legacyText.1905869632: “The line can't tell the difference,” Julian says.
legacyText.2401036404: I look down the long rows of names. People waiting for a call. People who refused one. People who once loved someone who used a system that couldn't bear an empty space. The bypass has turned a record into a place to hold them.
legacyText.3732816139: Wren presses her hands over her ears.
legacyText.1146761572: Imani takes her to the edge of a table, away from the nearest cables. Julian sets up the reader. Leila checks the receiving sequence against the original card. I follow Miso towards the inner room.
legacyText.3319312691: Mum is standing this time. She has wrapped a strip of cloth around her hand, but it has burned through in several places.
legacyText.2188284369: When she sees me, her face closes with fear before relief can reach it.
legacyText.2928049540: “I listened. Then we found the other reader.”
legacyText.2837382370: I tell her. Her eyes reach Voss before I finish.
legacyText.3794564656: “I have the revised sequence,” he says.
legacyText.1271728406: Mum looks at the bag, the brass box, Julian's grey hand. She understands more from those objects than I could have explained.
legacyText.2446181079: Then she looks back at me.
legacyText.1779723620: She accepts the answer. It costs her something; I can see it. I don't soften it before she has time to hear it.
legacyText.2065832976: I take her free hand again. This time I don't need to check whether the familiar rough patch is there. Her thumb closes over mine.
legacyText.2198454979: “No. I need to tell you this part properly. I tried. Then I stopped. Every time I thought I could make the next attempt safer, I found another reason to wait. At first it was the right decision. After a while I couldn't tell how much was right and how much was being afraid to hear you ask me to come home.”
legacyText.3927567941: Her voice breaks on the word. I look at the burned cloth around her other hand. I am angry with her and afraid for her at the same time, and neither feeling makes room for the other.
legacyText.230619371: Imani comes to the doorway. “We need to put the reader close enough to connect without pulling the hand control.”
legacyText.2485808977: Mum wipes her face with her sleeve. “Under the table. There's a shelf. Don't touch the left bracket.”
legacyText.1841011103: The instructions give her a way to stand upright again.
legacyText.1523689467: For ten minutes I work around her. Julian positions the reader. Imani passes the connectors in the order I rehearsed. Leila renews the holding marks without closing the release side. Miso moves along the floor, checking where the cables pass into the stone.
legacyText.3739332821: Voss stands by the master switch. He has the task he asked for and no private line to operate. I watch him whenever his hands move.
legacyText.509956767: Wren comes in last. Mum looks at her face, then at the card she is holding.
legacyText.288074000: “I didn't know what else to call what I was hearing.”
legacyText.3985162237: “I thought I could bring you there.”
legacyText.202383147: Mum looks at me, then down at the cable in her hand. “That was kind. It was also dangerous.”
legacyText.3275752713: Wren's mouth twists. “People can do both?”
legacyText.2160690450: “Yes,” Mum says. “I'm finding that very inconvenient.”
legacyText.1444475444: It is not a grand explanation. Wren seems to prefer it.
legacyText.1771944851: Julian checks the reader. The first indicator glows. The second remains dark.
legacyText.1940553917: “We need the actual receiving mark,” he says. “Nadia's. The one Adrian copied.”
legacyText.2685941490: Mum nods towards the back of the panel. “His version's there. Mine is underneath.”
legacyText.2348622441: I kneel and find the two layers. The false signature is visible on top. Beneath it, scratched into the brass, is the mark my mother drew before the bypass existed.
legacyText.3451049321: I copy it exactly. The final stroke curves left instead of right. A small error to build eleven months around.
legacyText.3334077367: Leila calls Dennis through the outer line.
legacyText.2289075312: At first the reader makes no sound. I can hear the click of the outer timer through Leila's phone, the shallow breathing of the people nearest me, and a relay moving under Nadia's table.
legacyText.4251064315: Then every label in the room turns towards the brass box.
legacyText.2340368105: I am not sure labels can turn. I watch the movement happen anyway, name after name lifting its lower edge as if caught by a wind I cannot feel.
legacyText.673677832: Julian puts his good hand on the lever.
legacyText.2842605521: The resistance is immediate. Not pain, exactly. The sense that a weight has been placed on the far end of a long tool I am trying to keep level. My fingers tighten around the chalk. I remember the torn papers on Julian's desk. The forty-one seconds. The way breathing stopped the pieces shaking.
legacyText.175373202: Wren lays her receiving card beside the reader. Her name appears on the blank indicator strip.
legacyText.3846812380: Mum starts to open her burned hand.
legacyText.1671851905: A cable jerks through the brass loop around her wrist. She cries out and closes her fingers again.
legacyText.1146480704: Julian lowers the lever. “Not yet. Something's still returning the refusal as a yes.”
legacyText.3523701985: Voss turns towards the master panel.
legacyText.3585596026: I see his hand stop over a switch he hasn't mentioned.
legacyText.90244587: “If we clear it, we lose the stored calls.”
legacyText.1725681383: He looks at Wren. The reader is pulling separate voices out of her shape; faces flicker across her skin, too fast to distinguish. At the centre, the face she chose is trying to hold still.
legacyText.280153344: I want to shout. I need the breath to hold the mark.
legacyText.2020065932: Imani steps between him and the switch. “You heard her leave.”
legacyText.2278579447: Voss takes out the photograph. I hadn't realised he still had it with him. He studies Eva's face as if the answer might be written somewhere the camera failed to focus.
legacyText.3739859861: Mum loosens one finger. Another cable slams against the table. The receiver count doubles.
legacyText.3085869094: Julian has one hand on the lever and the other held uselessly against his chest. He could slow the release, but not while he holds the reader aligned. Imani could reach him, but that would leave Voss alone at the master panel.
legacyText.835915713: Miso puts one paw beside the outer circle. Not inside it. He waits until I nod, then adds his weight to the connection. The trembling eases.
legacyText.4139040924: I have seconds in which I can think.
legacyText.644821500: The first option is to finish the separation. It needs a receiver who can remain distinct while the messages move, a route that recognises Wren, and another person to hold the reader steady. I have either earned those things or I haven't. Wanting them now won't put them in the room.
legacyText.987173680: The second is to break the bell. Leila can sever the crossing from outside while Nadia still has enough strength to leave. Wren's new record may hold her shape, but the unfinished voices will be cut away. Some will never reach the people waiting for them.
legacyText.1147421810: The third is to take the whole receiving load myself. Not replace Nadia under Voss's old instruction; choose a new, limited service and give the others time to disconnect. I would stay inside. They could build a way to reach me, but nobody here knows how to bring me home.
legacyText.4218838085: Mum sees where I am looking.
legacyText.1334841275: “You do not owe me that,” she says.
legacyText.2409048234: “You need to know before you choose.”
legacyText.1599068108: I look at her burned hand, at Julian's bandage, at the card Wren wrote her own name on. I look at Imani, who has been waiting for me to make a decision she can disagree with and still help me carry out.
legacyText.1607701585: I put the chalk against the last open line.
legacyText.1882204714: I look past him. Three passengers sit under advertisements for things I have never heard of. A woman with a cardboard suitcase is picking loose threads from her gloves. A boy in a school uniform holds a loaf of bread wrapped in a tea towel. Neither looks at me.
legacyText.2580217513: “That is something that happened. What did you leave?”
legacyText.1767679217: The doors wait. The woman stops picking her glove.
legacyText.738676291: I could say the flat. The answer is technically true. I could make a joke and see whether the driver has a sense of humour, though he hasn't offered much evidence.
legacyText.371639758: I look down at the chemistry worksheet still stuck to my boot by a strip of wet tape from the alley.
legacyText.1052120119: “I stopped putting her things back,” I say. “When my aunt tidied them away. I used to get them out again. Then it was easier not to.”
legacyText.2465079054: My voice has gone quieter than I want. I hope Imani won't turn towards me.
legacyText.12154978: The driver reaches for a pad of transfers. “Easier to sleep?”
legacyText.1696855629: He stamps the paper and gives it to me.
legacyText.4280563227: Miso puts his head out of my coat. “Anubis.”
legacyText.4019411445: The driver tips his cap. In the window beside him, his reflection has a long black muzzle and upright ears. I look at the real man, then back at the glass.
legacyText.2232871946: “Yes,” he says. “Please keep clear of the doors.”
legacyText.3227576594: I sit down with the transfer going damp in my hand. Imani sits beside me. For a whole block she says nothing.
legacyText.3805879321: Then she points at my boot.
legacyText.4043866905: I peel the worksheet off. Outside, the streetlights stop at the edge of a wide black river.
legacyText.822532824: Mum pushes me towards the door.
legacyText.2909467242: “Then you won't be able to come back.”
legacyText.1550966299: Imani drags Julian over the threshold. Miso lands beside them. My mother's hand is still on my coat.
legacyText.2659117724: I turn and put my hand over hers. One quick pressure. Then she lets go.
legacyText.2445156501: The door shuts against my shoulder.
legacyText.358847666: On the blank wall of the exchange room, I leave a streak of blood from my elbow and a white chalk mark that won't close.
legacyText.227098188: Afterwards, she takes off her helmet and runs a hand through flattened hair. There is a red mark across her forehead where the padding sat.
legacyText.1986577343: I think of the notebook and decide not to turn that into an observation.
legacyText.1351364312: Her dad goes to fetch the car. She sits beside me and starts undoing the fastening on a shin pad.
legacyText.3370416164: “I don't know. They don't tell you there.”
legacyText.1597395173: She looks at me. Then she laughs, a quick tired sound.
legacyText.1142567043: I show her Julian's messages. The smile leaves her face, but she doesn't stop undoing the fastening.
legacyText.243422820: “You can stop making everything a confession. I just asked.”
legacyText.3171080449: She pulls the pad free. Under it, her leg is bruised along the shin. I had been thinking of her as the person who arrived carrying a weapon. Looking at the marks, I begin to understand how much work came before she picked it up.
legacyText.57879296: Her dad brings the car around. Imani makes me sit in front because her bag occupies most of the back seat. As her dad drives towards the annex, the heater blows too hot on my wet boots.
legacyText.730291625: “What's wrong with the cat?” her dad asks suddenly.
legacyText.3704041011: “The black one. I saw it at the window yesterday. Didn't move for half an hour.”
legacyText.1697160033: I consider possible answers. “He's waiting for somebody.”
legacyText.2055828192: Her dad nods as if that makes sense.
legacyText.226515627: Outside the annex, he waits until Imani and I reach the door. She turns back and waves. He gives the short two-finger gesture I saw at the rink, then drives away.
legacyText.1210140314: Inside, Julian has covered an entire sheet with the same connector drawing. This time he has labelled the missing part.
legacyText.2384987868: I put my notebook beside it.
legacyText.3435801962: “Let's go home,” I say. “Properly. All of us.”
legacyText.3659882742: I answer before the second ring.
legacyText.404822539: For a moment all I hear is someone breathing too close to a microphone. I am about to ask who it is when the person outside knocks. The breath on the line catches at exactly the same time as mine.
legacyText.2061792168: I don't say my name. I learned that much from a school assembly about scams, though the person giving the assembly did not discuss visitors wearing my face.
legacyText.585584626: I put the phone on the counter. I want both hands free. I don't know what I expect to do with them.
legacyText.2338267445: I hold the power button until the screen goes black. For two seconds the flat is quiet.
legacyText.4035544881: Then the phone rings again. The screen stays dark.
legacyText.1184478582: I put it on the counter and step away. This feels like the sort of thing that should solve a problem if I do it decisively enough. It doesn't.
legacyText.2709597701: The third knock comes from the door.
legacyText.1044691525: A voice from the black phone says, ‘{{firstName}}? Please. I know you can hear it.’
legacyText.1296055139: I recognise the voice, and that is worse than not recognising it.
legacyText.644173700: Eventually I touch the screen. It lights up with the same call still waiting, as though the phone has simply refused to take part in my decision. I answer without putting it to my ear.
legacyText.1363177270: ‘I'm going to need help,’ I tell Imani. ‘I don't know what kind yet.’
legacyText.2367748490: She looks towards the road. ‘Then don't tell me I have to. Ask.’
legacyText.1182991429: ‘Yes.’ She checks the map on her phone. ‘And I'm telling my dad where we are.’
legacyText.1326247104: ‘You can carry your own phone when you grow thumbs,’ she tells him.
legacyText.765719785: He looks offended. I leave them to establish their own relationship.
legacyText.3942103679: ‘Just keep up,’ I say. ‘I'll explain when I can.’
legacyText.3776815251: I get three steps farther before noticing. When I turn, she is still standing by the bins.
legacyText.1854844331: I look at the map on my phone. I don't know whether the next street is the safe one. She doesn't either. That is not a reason to pretend she agreed to be instructed.
legacyText.3920223048: ‘Will you come to the annex?’ I ask.
legacyText.3310935662: She considers it. ‘Your aunt asked me to check on you. I'm doing that. We'll see after.’
legacyText.87429753: She walks beside me, leaving more space than before.
legacyText.2045561366: ‘Tell me what the transfer gives you before I pay,’ I say.
legacyText.3310031805: The driver's hand remains open. ‘A record that you entered this road willingly. No claim on your return. No permission to speak for you.’
legacyText.306160671: ‘Only the account needed for the crossing.’
legacyText.1103281444: I think about it, then tell him I left a kitchen where my mother's things have begun to look like somebody else's clutter. I don't give him every memory attached to that sentence.
legacyText.4216396354: He stamps the transfer and gives it to me. ‘Defined terms,’ he says. ‘A useful habit.’
legacyText.2316513335: Imani puts her fare away. ‘We're keeping that habit.’
legacyText.4030273339: We sit down together. Miso climbs out of my collar, dislodging a considerable amount of fur onto my coat.
legacyText.3137259605: In the window, my reflection smiles. I haven't moved my mouth.
legacyText.2037199921: The driver closes his hand. ‘Then I cannot issue the transfer.’
legacyText.745161050: The doors remain open. Beyond them, the staircase is visible. I can get there, but it will not count as a witnessed crossing.
legacyText.152185762: I feel a moment of triumph, followed by the uncomfortable recognition that I have won nothing except permission to leave without the thing I need.
legacyText.1726394747: Imani steps down first. She does not look at me until both feet are on the concrete.
legacyText.2047401947: Miso follows, saying nothing at all.
legacyText.900089417: I try to push past the driver's arm.
legacyText.201617364: I do not get far. The space beyond the fare reader lengthens while my feet stay where they are. My elbow strikes the rail hard enough to make my fingers numb.
legacyText.1834584059: ‘You may refuse passage,’ he says. ‘You may not turn everyone else's road into your entrance.’
legacyText.191383396: Imani takes my good arm and pulls me back. I let her. The shame comes before the pain, which is an unpleasant order for either feeling.
legacyText.711037407: At the next ordinary landing, the doors open. No transfer. No blessing. A way out which remains a way out because he said it would.
legacyText.2407713137: On the concrete, I unwrap the dressing at my elbow and see fresh blood. Imani has stopped asking whether it hurts.
legacyText.3688936155: ‘I don't want to give you that,’ I say.
legacyText.3716491247: The driver inclines his head. ‘Then use the exit.’
legacyText.3233096097: I expected an argument. Getting none makes me hesitate.
legacyText.974134394: Imani steps down beside me. Miso follows. The streetcar remains until I am clear of the doors, then moves away across the river.
legacyText.2139238071: ‘We still reach the exchange room?’ I ask.
legacyText.4252410225: ‘We walk farther,’ Miso says. ‘Not every refusal ends the road.’
