legacyText.1802864019: The steps are steep and my boots are wet. I spend the climb thinking about the question I chose not to answer. I don't decide whether I should have answered it. I am glad the decision was allowed to remain mine.
legacyText.3447386793: I show Imani the back of the photograph before putting the notebook away.
legacyText.2800727392: ‘Those were under Eva's name,’ I say. ‘I copied the crossed-out one too.’
legacyText.542128739: She takes a picture of my page, discovers the photograph comes out blank, and writes the numbers into her own notebook instead.
legacyText.993423786: ‘Two copies,’ she says. ‘If one of us drops something off another roof.’
legacyText.2284325793: I laugh. When the fear returns, I don't have to carry the information alone with it.
legacyText.3534255016: I close the notebook before Imani can see the back of the photograph.
legacyText.1241233711: ‘Anything else he gave you?’ she asks.
legacyText.1352252546: The word comes easily. I tell myself I am checking the numbers before worrying anyone. I tell myself I will share them when they make sense.
legacyText.3048051558: Imani watches me put the notebook away.
legacyText.3814031820: I had wanted the lie to end the question. It does. That is not as reassuring as I expected.
legacyText.1146501622: I slide the evidence across the desk.
legacyText.526617321: Thoth gives me a receipt with a clear list of what he is retaining. I check the recorder's serial number, though I have never cared about a serial number in my life. Julian checks it too.
legacyText.1655716081: ‘Copies remain yours,’ Thoth says. ‘The correction will show both the false entry and the evidence against it.’
legacyText.563276612: I nod. I am not buying the disappearance of a bad fact. I am making it possible for someone else to see what happened.
legacyText.2315979468: It shuts before I can lift it. My sleeve is caught between the covers. The third pen stops above the page, perfectly still.
legacyText.3905831702: ‘You came to challenge a stolen authority.’
legacyText.2213379712: I let go. The sleeve comes free with a neat tear along the seam.
legacyText.3216400322: Julian has gone pale. Imani steps back from the desk. I cannot think of an answer that makes the last five seconds look better.
legacyText.2022083808: Thoth copies the public route reference onto a card and puts it beyond my reach. ‘You may take the address. You may not use my witness seal.’
legacyText.4161631106: I take the card only after he nods. The walk to the stairs feels very long.
legacyText.4120361630: Thoth withdraws the evidence form. ‘Then I cannot certify the correction.’
legacyText.3120540648: He considers the reference number, then writes a public routing entry on a card. ‘A destination. Not proof of your authority to change what happens there.’
legacyText.3477495867: I take it. My mother's voice remains in my pocket. The witness receipt stays on his desk.
legacyText.457887151: Julian does not tell me that I chose badly. He asks me to put the difference in the notebook so nobody later assumes I have something I don't.
legacyText.1302356025: I grab Julian's sleeve and pull.
legacyText.3072543963: He comes away from the panel with a sharp cry. His hand has gone grey to the wrist. I get his good arm over my shoulder and take his weight before my injured elbow can object.
legacyText.1294522643: Behind him, the spare connector remains in the socket. I see it. I know it might have helped. I keep moving.
legacyText.2384329167: Julian tries to say my name. I tell him to save the breath until he is through the door.
legacyText.3792743329: Imani takes his other side. Together we get him over the threshold.
legacyText.1776020851: I reach for the spare connector.
legacyText.1604453603: The metal is hot enough to burn through my glove. I pull it free and fall against the panel. Behind me, Imani swears and hauls Julian away from the closing contact.
legacyText.461977624: I turn. His injured hand hangs at a wrong, stiff angle. She has his good arm over her shoulder, carrying a weight I chose not to reach first.
legacyText.3821297700: I help them through the door with the connector burning in my pocket. It may be useful. It doesn't make Imani meet my eyes.
legacyText.3950850388: Julian says, ‘You got it, then,’ in a voice I cannot read.
legacyText.3912269247: For the rest of the session I watch the puck closely enough to lose it twice. I don't understand every decision Imani makes, but I begin to recognise when she's pleased with one.
legacyText.393790703: When she looks towards the benches again, I am still there.
legacyText.4071015635: The archive message can wait until the whistle. I don't pretend waiting was easy. It matters that I chose it anyway.
legacyText.2400685528: I show Imani's dad the message and say I need to go. He nods, distracted by a shot at the far end of the rink.
legacyText.423484491: Outside, I call Leila before going to the flat. She meets me there. Together we find the manual before Imani's session finishes. It is a useful hour. I keep telling myself that while looking at my phone.
legacyText.2776088906: Imani's message arrives at eleven thirty: “Went looking for you. Dad said you had another thing.”
legacyText.2016482228: I start an explanation, delete half of it and send the plain version: I left to find the manual. Should've told you myself.
legacyText.1041404711: Her reply comes several minutes later. Yes.
legacyText.949778801: When she joins me at the flat, she asks to read the diagram before agreeing to the next part of the plan.
legacyText.1898022507: ‘You don't have to keep us here,’ I tell the girl. ‘What happens if we leave?’
legacyText.2703385924: She looks at the door. ‘He asks why I let you.’
legacyText.2371374196: I don't tell her it will. Instead I ask whether she wants to come as far as the window and see the roof herself.
legacyText.24150818: She moves aside. Only a little. Enough to let Imani reach the catch without pushing past her.
legacyText.4055560370: ‘Voss said to let us take the reader,’ I say. ‘It's part of the test.’
legacyText.1827388984: The girl's face brightens with relief. Then it tightens.
legacyText.3507109783: I point towards the door. ‘Ask him.’
legacyText.3856550867: She turns for long enough that Imani can reach the window. I have bought a few seconds by making another person doubt what she was told.
legacyText.2412920636: When the girl turns back, she knows. I can see it before she speaks.
legacyText.4275224401: The cable nearest my boot coils tightly enough to crack the floor tile.
legacyText.3093889761: I swing the torch towards her hand, trying to knock the cable away.
legacyText.4159586733: It goes through her wrist. The force of my own movement pulls me off balance. I hit the cupboard hard with my injured elbow.
legacyText.1213962039: The girl looks down at the place I tried to strike. Her face becomes my mother's for one terrible second.
legacyText.228328568: ‘Don't,’ Imani says. I'm not sure which of us she means.
legacyText.1978397210: I get up. The torch has broken against the wood. The girl steps back from me, opening a path without offering trust.
legacyText.2098276128: Outside the door, Voss begins turning the handle.
legacyText.2941755721: ‘We're taking the reader,’ I say. ‘I'm not making a deal about my mother.’
legacyText.2387381651: The girl watches me. ‘I wasn't asking for her.’
legacyText.3873466561: I look at the cable in her hand and realise I heard a threat before she made one.
legacyText.2535046983: She steps away from the window. ‘You can. I don't have to like it.’
legacyText.1371414402: Imani opens the catch. Cold air moves through the room. I keep watching the girl's face, expecting another borrowed one. It stays her own unfinished shape.
legacyText.838704101: For once, nobody makes the refusal mean more than it does.
legacyText.1286469902: I offer the witness papers with my hands open.
legacyText.2836197: ‘Passage for those who choose it. Return for the same people, if they choose to leave. No replacement required.’
legacyText.580732244: Wepwawet examines the receiving record. He looks at Wren, not at me.
legacyText.1960508720: The standard lifts. The stone doors part far enough for the equipment bag.
legacyText.2770010330: ‘The road is open,’ he says. ‘Keep the terms you named.’
legacyText.4125076512: I step through without trying to take a piece of the opening with me.
legacyText.3682816467: ‘Wepwawet,’ I say, carefully. ‘Opener of the Ways. I ask for a road, not control of it.’
legacyText.1430728797: His shadow moves before he does. For a moment the jackal on the standard seems larger than the room.
legacyText.1766914093: ‘You know which work you are asking for.’
legacyText.2293552312: I show him the page in Nadia's notebook. He reads the little correction beside the sketch.
legacyText.3928884617: He turns the standard aside. The gap widens. Knowledge has not made him mine to command; it has let me make a request he can recognise.
legacyText.2884330469: Wren goes through beside me, holding her card in one hand.
legacyText.68437110: The standard strikes the floor. The sound knocks the breath from my lungs. I land on my knees, skin burning where the stone scrapes through my jeans.
legacyText.1043216881: Wepwawet has not struck me. He has stopped the road moving with me on it. The distinction does not improve the pain.
legacyText.4174982771: Imani puts the equipment bag down before helping me stand.
legacyText.846878813: ‘You have a route back,’ the god says. ‘Take it if you will not ask for passage.’
legacyText.3030382356: I look at the blood on my knee, then at the person holding the door.
legacyText.4196062210: ‘Passage,’ I say. The word is difficult to get out. ‘For everyone who chooses it.’
legacyText.2728320582: He waits until I have named the return terms too. Only then does the opening widen.
legacyText.604362629: I refuse the terms and take the upper stair with the others. Wepwawet does not stop me.
legacyText.1096574793: Miso finds an old maintenance return halfway up, a route Adrian once used before the stone doors were installed. It is narrow, flooded and no longer held level. I can reach the lower station, but I won't arrive on a recognised road.
legacyText.290994252: The first section is almost ordinary. Then the water rises to my knees. Imani carries the reader above her head while Julian keeps the receiving card dry inside his coat. I use two holding marks to cross a place where the floor has gone. One collapses before I finish. I strike my knee against a submerged step and keep moving because stopping would leave the person behind me without a place to put their foot.
legacyText.1084440374: At the lower end, Miso opens a service panel. I climb into the station soaked, late and unwitnessed. I did not have to accept the god's terms. I have paid for the other road with time and a knee that will not take my full weight.
legacyText.2120653996: Imani puts the reader down carefully. “We do not pretend that was free,” she says. I nod before trying to stand.
legacyText.568789819: I ask another question. Wren looks at the empty glove on the floor. “I heard you,” she says. “I said not yet.” I begin to explain the deadline. Imani sets the cracker packet down hard enough that I stop. Nobody has to shout for the room to become uncomfortable. I back away from the question, but Wren keeps watching my hands for the rest of the test.
legacyText.974267008: I put the tested clay figures along the reader’s supports. Each carries one defined segment, then stops. The rehearsal gives me a way to share a load nobody could safely hold alone.
legacyText.3296260330: I fit the spare connector into the reader’s empty brace. The component I took gives the load another point of support. Julian checks it carefully before trusting his injured hand near it.
legacyText.490257567: “Clear it,” I tell Voss. “Then leave the switch.”
legacyText.2425691467: Wren turns towards him. For a moment she is Eva, exactly as she stood in the photograph. I see Voss's whole body lean forward.
legacyText.3171678802: Then Wren returns to her own face.
legacyText.4265319146: “I could keep doing that,” she says. “Would you ever stop asking?”
legacyText.2980809343: He looks at the photograph. At the master panel. At Nadia, trying not to cry out while another cable pulls against her hand.
legacyText.2666400925: At last he opens the cache switch.
legacyText.2521518533: The photograph tears across its folded crease. He catches both halves and holds them together, although the picture no longer lines up.
legacyText.3970493062: The count on the reader drops.
legacyText.435905570: She moves towards the reader, then stops where I need her. The support comes from the work I prepared and the person still willing to hold the other end. Voss stays where Dennis's voice through the phone tells him to stay. It is an arrangement nobody would have believed possible two days ago.
legacyText.1872154472: I open the release side of the mark.
legacyText.2614960650: The first voice is a man's. He asks whether his brother collected the tools from the shed. It is so ordinary I almost laugh. Wren looks at the label turning towards her, then at the receiving indicator. A light flashes. The man says thank you, impatiently, as if everyone has taken too long about a simple errand.
legacyText.792348570: A second voice follows. Then four. Then enough that I can't separate the words. Wren can. I can see the work in the way she holds her shoulders, the careful pauses between one acknowledgement and the next.
legacyText.2963384772: Leila reaches her first. She doesn't pull. She slides a clean piece of cloth under the burned palm and supports the wrist while the cable loosens.
legacyText.3191927516: “Later,” Leila says. Her voice is shaking. “Do that later.”
legacyText.3454378511: Mum laughs once and starts crying. The brass loop opens. Her hand comes free.
legacyText.633292981: For a second I nearly let go of the chalk.
legacyText.46861876: Imani says my name sharply. I breathe and hold the mark.
legacyText.964937562: Wren is fading at the edges. Her card remains solid on the table, a small plain rectangle amid the moving light.
legacyText.3596829676: “Where do you want to stand?” I ask her.
legacyText.767898173: She looks at the doorway. At the strip of lake visible beyond it. At Miso's paw beside my chalk circle.
legacyText.3261595389: She presses one hand to the card. Her face steadies.
legacyText.1709537908: A woman speaks through the reader. I recognise Mrs. Bell's voice before the name turns towards me. She does not ask about a pharmacy this time.
legacyText.1385560441: The letter in my notebook grows warm. Somewhere far above me, a receiving line opens for one message. I don't hear the rest. It isn't addressed to me.
legacyText.3214730334: Miso lifts his paw. I hold the connection alone for the last few seconds.
legacyText.2191469611: The final voice is very quiet. A girl says, “You can put it down now.”
legacyText.478754476: Voss closes his eyes. He doesn't answer. He doesn't reach for a switch. He folds the two halves of the photograph together and lowers his hands.
legacyText.2976404031: The labels settle. The cables hang loose. The weight at the far end of my mark lifts so suddenly that I fall onto one knee.
legacyText.484186645: Imani catches the chalk before it rolls under the table.
legacyText.2849063275: He checks the indicator, then checks it again because he doesn't trust a first answer anymore.
legacyText.2163806114: Wren stands beside the reader with her hands on the table. She is still there. Her coat is too big. One glove is missing. Her face is hers.
legacyText.3329356552: Mum takes a step towards me and almost falls. Leila catches her under one arm. I take the other side, feeling the weight of her ordinary body for the first time since she disappeared.
legacyText.3228428192: Miso heads for the stairs without waiting to be told. Wren picks her card up carefully and follows him. Julian carries the reader with both hands; his grey fingers have begun to take colour around the knuckles.
legacyText.2795668596: Voss remains beside the master panel.
legacyText.698830099: He nods. Picks up the empty equipment bag. Follows.
legacyText.195532970: At the staircase, Mum stops to look back once. I let her. Then I put my hand over hers and help her towards the light.
legacyText.1637055360: At the top of the stairs, Dennis gives Mum a blanket before he asks her name. She holds it around her shoulders with the good hand and looks at the ordinary wall behind her as if she can't believe it has stopped being a doorway.
legacyText.163482373: Leila phones for an ambulance. This part she knows how to do. She gives the location, the injuries, the number of people who need assessment. She does not start with the impossible explanation.
legacyText.23316585: Voss sits on a low concrete step. When the police arrive, he gets up without being asked. Leila tells them he has information about Nadia's disappearance and unsafe equipment in two buildings. There will be time later to work out which words can fit in a statement. For now, she gives names and addresses and makes sure they are written down.
legacyText.1172355742: I hear her say, “I'm safe,” then, “I know,” then, “I can't explain all of it over the phone.” She keeps the call going until he reaches her. When he arrives, he hugs her so tightly her feet move off the ground.
legacyText.2221353100: Mum watches them. I stand beside her, close enough that my sleeve touches the blanket.
legacyText.921635139: She looks at me, uncertain for the first time in a way that has nothing to do with the machinery.
legacyText.1874147679: I move first. She wraps the blanket around both of us. Her shoulder is thinner than I remember. I press my face into it and finally stop keeping track of who is watching.
legacyText.3765748903: At the hospital, the receptionist asks whether Nadia has identification. Leila produces a folder. Of course she brought a folder. I begin laughing and can't stop until it turns into something else.
legacyText.3589135395: Wren waits with Imani in a row of plastic chairs. A nurse asks whether she is family. Wren looks at the card in her hand, then at me.
legacyText.2244850282: “Yes,” I say, and then stop before deciding for her. “If she wants.”
legacyText.274153219: Wren thinks about it. “I can wait.”
legacyText.1485135518: The nurse gives her a visitor sticker. Wren spends the next hour peeling one corner up and pressing it down again, fascinated by how it stays when she chooses not to hold it.
legacyText.2791128766: Julian's hand has regained most of its colour. He still can't bend two fingers properly. Leila makes sure somebody examines them rather than accepting that magical damage must require magical neglect.
legacyText.923100024: Miso stays outside the hospital doors. I find him under a bench when I come out for air. His bare neck looks strangely small without the collar.
legacyText.3630953353: He looks at me. Then at the hospital entrance.
legacyText.3595292251: I sit on the bench. The sun has risen. I missed the moment it happened.
legacyText.3373136031: My phone is full of ordinary notifications: school messages, a discount code, somebody replying to a group chat that has carried on without knowing anything about my weekend. I read each one because I can.
legacyText.117311444: Under them is a new draft call. No number. No caller ID.
legacyText.614630223: I don't press it yet. I take the phone inside, where Mum can see it too.
legacyText.2141801982: When Imani talks about selection, she reminds me she looked for me after the first session. I listen before offering to come to the next one.
legacyText.1543718668: Mum borrows a pen from the nurse and draws the return circuit on the back of a hospital menu. The soup choices get in the way. She works around them.
legacyText.1892924504: “The first connection kept a route back to where the claim began. It couldn't close while the receiving instruction was still active.”
legacyText.3652608076: “I'm saying you can. I don't know whether you have to.”
legacyText.1738165653: The distinction feels like something I learned on the stairs: an open road doesn't decide whether I use it.
legacyText.3424761107: I look at the draft call. Friday, 02:13. My kitchen. The chair at the table. The version of me who hasn't yet learned which details will become important.
legacyText.1353596330: I could tell myself everything. The bell, the notebook, the false signature. I try to imagine receiving that list from an unknown caller and remember how close I came to turning the phone off. Maybe a message can only carry what the person on the other end can hold.
legacyText.764768980: Mum hands back the phone. She doesn't tell me what to choose.
legacyText.2161997170: For one ring I hear nothing. Then the line opens to the sound of my own frightened breathing.
legacyText.2478162686: I press my free hand against the hospital chair.
legacyText.3304954753: “Whatever happens,” I say, “do not open the door.”
legacyText.2425019375: At the other end, a chair scrapes across laminate.
legacyText.2173799197: My own voice, younger by two days and a great deal else.
legacyText.1628262073: I sit with the phone still against my ear. Mum's good hand rests on my sleeve.
legacyText.1411581281: “What were you going to say?” she asks.
legacyText.555621670: I look at the hospital menu with its impossible diagram. The floor outside the curtain. My aunt returning with tea she will insist somebody drinks before it gets cold.
legacyText.1683840847: Mum rubs her thumb across the worn bird patch on my coat.
legacyText.1391716332: Three weeks later, the flat contains more people than it has chairs. Julian brings a folding one from the archive, which he says should not leave the building and has therefore labelled with the building's name in case that helps.
legacyText.1870480249: Leila makes dinner. Mum tries to help and is told to sit down. They argue for four minutes about whether chopping one onion counts as rest. I let them. I hadn't realised I missed being annoyed by both of them at once.
legacyText.1225063974: Voss is under investigation. There are statements about Nadia's disappearance, equipment records, unsafe access and financial arrangements nobody in my kitchen is qualified to explain. His wife has asked for the original recording of Eva's call. Julian sends a copy through a solicitor. I don't hear what she says when she receives it. I don't need to.
legacyText.2970629933: Mum goes to appointments. Some days her hand hurts too much to hold a pen. Some nights she knocks on my bedroom door to make sure I'm there, then pretends she needed to borrow a charger. I stop pretending to believe her and let her sit for a while.
legacyText.3381230938: Leila and I do not repair everything in one conversation. She starts telling me when she doesn't know something. I start telling her before leaving the building. It is inconvenient for both of us. We keep doing it.
legacyText.3610950392: Wren has been living in the annex's spare room while people work out what papers the ordinary world will accept. She comes over wearing a coat that fits. She has learned to dislike olives and asks whether this is a personality or just a food opinion.
legacyText.138636437: “Both, if you mention it often enough,” Imani tells her.
legacyText.2062729851: Julian has called his sister. He didn't get the wedding back. He told her why the photographs had become homework. I don't know how much she believed. I know he is going to her house on Sunday and bringing a cake he has been instructed not to choose himself.
legacyText.1281463233: Miso sleeps on my chemistry textbook. I move him only when absolutely necessary, which he defines differently from me.
legacyText.3526893832: After dinner, Imani stays to help clear the table. Her phone lights up with a message from the selection coach. She reads it twice, then hands me the screen without speaking.
legacyText.408679094: I read the message. Look at her. She is trying very hard not to smile before I do.
legacyText.559672042: She grins properly then. I shout for Leila, who comes in carrying a wet plate and complains that I frightened her before joining the celebration.
legacyText.3556968072: Later, when everyone has gone, I find a small paper bird on the fire escape. Wren made it from the blank end of an old archive form. Its wings are uneven. I bring it inside and put it beside Mum's blue notebook.
legacyText.4201795946: Imani. She left her gloves under the chair, and she would like I to stop telling people she cried at the message, because she didn't.
legacyText.3327345438: I look towards the kitchen, where Mum is trying to make toast without setting off the alarm.
legacyText.1374384913: She looks at the reader, then at Nadia's hand. I see her understand the whole choice before she speaks into the phone.
legacyText.2356259364: “Sever the outer circuit. On my count.”
legacyText.3574536576: Wren takes one step away from the table.
legacyText.956551355: It is the hardest answer I have given her.
legacyText.2723942302: Imani goes to her side. “You can hold my hand if you want.”
legacyText.498068111: Wren nods. The borrowed faces move more slowly across her skin, as if the voices are listening too.
legacyText.2885235187: Julian makes sure the second reader is detached from the main line. His good hand is precise. His injured one shakes.
legacyText.3077755738: Mum opens two fingers. The cable jerks. I add the last of the chalk to the holding mark and press the point down hard enough to hurt.
legacyText.632021444: Through Leila's phone comes a sharp metal crack.
legacyText.3950554109: Nothing happens for half a second. Then every label in the room lifts at once.
legacyText.2267265203: The sound is not a scream. It is thousands of unfinished syllables cut short, words losing their ends. A request, an apology, somebody asking where a book has been put. I hear fragments and understand none of them well enough to keep.
legacyText.64751991: Leila pulls the brass loop open with both hands. Nadia cries out. I turn towards her and miss the moment Wren falls.
legacyText.767339641: Imani catches her before she reaches the floor. Wren's face has gone pale and difficult to see. Her receiving card lies on the table. I pick it up and put it in her hand.
legacyText.3514341829: I say it again, not as an order, just as the name I know belongs to the person in front of me.
legacyText.3621321451: Her fingers close over the card.
legacyText.2661417898: For several seconds, all of us wait. I can hear Mum breathing behind me, uneven and too fast. Julian has put the reader down to kneel beside Imani. Miso stands at Wren's feet, his back arched.
legacyText.4257711230: Nobody tries to tell her that's good.
legacyText.3883201442: The station begins to change. Without the connections holding its different parts together, the rooms no longer fit. The doorway to Nadia's table becomes a narrow arch. The far switchboard slides towards a wall which wasn't there before.
legacyText.2483244288: He doesn't wait for agreement. He lifts the reader, checks that Imani has Wren, and moves towards the stairs. I help Leila support Nadia. Miso leads, stopping whenever the floor changes under his paws.
legacyText.1827106093: Voss stands alone beside the master panel. The switches have gone dark. He is pressing one with the end of his thumb, over and over, without enough force to move it.
legacyText.2868649754: He doesn't hear me. Or he does and doesn't know what to do with the words.
legacyText.1287410066: I go back far enough to take his sleeve.
legacyText.394557933: He looks down at my hand. Then at the empty panel. He comes without resisting.
legacyText.29194084: On the first landing, the wall of water moves inward. I feel cold drops on my face. Imani shifts Wren's arm higher across her shoulders and keeps climbing. Julian goes backwards up two steps so he can guide her feet.
legacyText.1744524313: The lower station folds away beneath me.
legacyText.2711675919: I don't watch it go. My mother is heavy against my side, and every time she breathes I can feel her ribs move through the coat.
legacyText.3890508093: At the top, Dennis stands beside a bell broken into two uneven pieces. The button has rolled under his chair.
legacyText.1862699486: He looks at the people coming through the door and counts silently. I see his lips move.
legacyText.2220571893: Leila looks back at the narrowing stair.
legacyText.2594712494: It is accurate. I hear the part it leaves out.
legacyText.2191186456: For the first hour, Wren cannot bear to have anyone speak behind her. She turns at every sound, checking that it comes from a single mouth.
legacyText.3063866931: Imani sits where she can be seen. Julian brings water. Leila checks Nadia's burns, then Wren's hands, though there are no marks she knows how to treat.
legacyText.1720283583: Voss asks whether he can speak to Wren. She says no. He sits on the far side of the service room until the police come.
legacyText.1222017194: I tell them which buildings to check. Leila gives the statements she can make without guessing. Dennis shows them the broken bell. I keep thinking of the names in the lower station, trying to remember more than fragments.
legacyText.2058073134: At the hospital, Mum falls asleep halfway through asking a question. I sit beside the bed with her good hand between both of mine. When a nurse needs to check her blood pressure, I stand up too quickly and nearly fall.
legacyText.3882915099: I want to tell her that food isn't going to address the situation. Then I remember Leila has been saying similar things for eleven months, and I go to find a sandwich.
legacyText.1248313061: Wren is sitting by the window. She has removed the visitor sticker because the name field was blank. Julian gives her a pen. She writes WREN in large careful letters and puts the sticker back.
legacyText.2658921273: “You can say you don't know without looking like you're asking me to fix it.”
legacyText.1165830905: I sit down at the other end of the row. Outside, a hospital shuttle waits with its engine running.
legacyText.2272386144: “I keep trying to remember the names.”
legacyText.3072006840: Wren looks out of the window. “I remember some.”
legacyText.3267794451: When Imani's dad arrives, she goes to him at once. I watch them through the glass panel in the corridor door. She is speaking quickly, trying to explain enough. He listens with one hand on the back of her head.
legacyText.1580848696: Mum wakes in the afternoon. She asks for me, then for Leila, then whether everyone got out. I give her the answer Dennis got.
legacyText.2575727486: She closes her eyes. “That's not a small thing.”
legacyText.3317935981: I do know. I also know why it doesn't feel like enough.
legacyText.3197265429: On my phone, the last unknown call has vanished from the log. In its place is an unsent return connection. The destination is Friday, 02:13.
legacyText.180442259: I show it to Mum. She studies the screen for a long time.
legacyText.815316465: “The route was made before it broke,” she says. “One message. If you want.”
legacyText.1396161392: I look at her, lying in a hospital bed in Toronto. Alive. I look at the numberless call and think about what I could have said to the person I was two days ago.
legacyText.1727537192: I take the unsent call into an empty part of the corridor. The hospital is beginning its evening routine. Visitors put on coats. Staff change shifts. Somebody wheels a cart past me and says excuse me twice before I notice I'm in the way.
legacyText.3198376990: I sit down where I can see Mum's curtain.
legacyText.2803441072: The destination waits on the screen. Friday, 02:13. I remember what the voice said. I remember the terror of hearing myself from a day that hadn't arrived. The reserved date on the line was never the date of the speaker. It was the next place the old receiving instruction could put a message.
legacyText.2361333991: Now I can give it the voice it was waiting for.
legacyText.1423815811: “Whatever happens,” I say when the call connects, “do not open the door.”
legacyText.233166024: I hear myself move in the kitchen. I give the instruction about the notebook. I start to say one more thing, and the line ends.
legacyText.844228686: For a long time I look at the dark screen.
legacyText.1756832374: I want to believe the warning could make the ending different. That another version of me could find one more piece, persuade one more person, hold the chalk a little steadier. I cannot send a second call. The socket is closed.
legacyText.174275011: Three weeks later, Wren and I sit in the annex with a stack of blank cards. She names the voices she remembers. I write them down. Sometimes she knows a whole name and a sentence. Sometimes only a sound. I leave spaces instead of filling them with guesses.
legacyText.2745019492: The letter from Mrs. Bell lies beside the cards. Its address has faded but remains legible where Imani copied it. Whether I deliver it or keep it waiting is a decision the broken bell can no longer make for me.
legacyText.2247789301: Mum comes to help when her hand allows it. She is home now. The phrase still catches me by surprise. I hear her drop a spoon in the kitchen and feel relief before irritation can reach the sound.
legacyText.1475054847: Her return does not arrive as one clean happy thing. There are appointments, police interviews, questions from school and neighbours. She tires quickly. I get angry over small things because the large ones are hard to begin. Once I snap at her for moving my notebook, and she puts it back without telling me how lucky I am to have her there. Later, I apologise for the way I said it. I don't apologise for needing my things left alone.
legacyText.323250507: Leila has started using a shared calendar. She calls it practical. I suspect it is also her way of letting me see the plans before they become instructions. I put my own appointments in, reluctantly. Neither of us celebrates this development out loud.
legacyText.896465443: Wren is quieter than she was before the bell broke. She no longer changes faces when she is frightened. Instead she goes very still and asks people to stop talking for a minute. Usually they do. She is learning which people need reminding.
legacyText.1169058664: Julian's hand is recovering. He has told his sister about the wedding memory. She sent him a voice message three minutes long, mostly calling him an idiot and asking when he was coming round. He keeps it backed up in three places.
legacyText.3509826095: Imani has a decision from the selection coach. She tells me in person. I go to her next session and sit at the right end of the rink this time, where she can see me without turning her head too far.
legacyText.2654482466: Voss does not come to the annex. His part in Nadia's disappearance and the dangerous equipment is being investigated. I don't know whether any ordinary court can account for the rest. I know Leila gave them every record she could explain, including her own signature on the early tests.
legacyText.661676885: One evening, Wren stops halfway through a name.
legacyText.3625856937: I look at the cards. At the spaces I left.
legacyText.2785103587: She nods, but she isn't entirely reassured. I don't add a prettier sentence to make myself feel more helpful.
legacyText.3676071977: At home, Mum has burned the toast. The alarm is going off. Miso is shouting from the windowsill as if he has personally discovered a fire nobody else has noticed.
legacyText.1214842885: I open the kitchen window. Cold air enters. The alarm stops.
legacyText.1699581142: Mum stands in the middle of the room holding a plate with two black rectangles on it.
legacyText.677443769: She looks offended for a second, then laughs. I put the plate in the sink and get out the cereal.
legacyText.3647954129: My phone rings. A schoolfriend, asking whether I want the notes from chemistry. I look at Mum. She nods towards it and goes to fill the kettle.
legacyText.849991906: I ask Julian to describe the choice one more time.
legacyText.1854696336: He looks at Mum. At Leila. At Imani, who has gone very still.
legacyText.2547898869: “One receiver,” he says. “No forced continuation. We disconnect every other claim. The station becomes a place you operate, not a place that owns everyone attached to it.”
legacyText.1194992002: Mum says my name. I turn towards her. She is trying to let go of the cable, trying to make the other choice possible before I finish considering this one.
legacyText.1723884629: “Don't do it because you're my child,” she says.
legacyText.2192105847: I kneel beside the panel. I could still break the bell. That choice remains. The thought helps me keep the next words steady.
legacyText.999805319: Julian lowers the lever enough to open a blank receiving line.
legacyText.548585262: I take the brass feather from the box. Mum's fingers close around my wrist.
legacyText.2657879412: For a moment I stay like that, neither pulling away nor giving in. Her hand is warm above the burned cloth. I want another hour in the kitchen. I want her to complain about my hair again.
legacyText.1097463920: “I need you to keep looking,” I tell her.
legacyText.2847052814: She closes her eyes. When she opens them, there is no agreement in her face. There is understanding, which is different and harder to accept.
legacyText.2529087846: I write my name beside the new receiving slot. Then I say what I accept, as carefully as Leila taught me to define a connection. Only the waiting messages. No authority over their senders. No new compulsory calls. A line that can be reached from outside without placing the caller under claim.
legacyText.3133610978: The feather warms in my hand.
legacyText.518699200: Julian records each condition. Wren repeats it, listening for a response the rest of us cannot distinguish. Imani checks the page before letting me move to the next line.
legacyText.129825095: I close the holding mark around myself.
legacyText.2378432062: The load arrives slowly enough for me to know I could still stop before the second stage. I say that aloud. Julian confirms it. I take one more breath.
legacyText.516160997: She folds to the floor. Leila catches her. I want to go to them, but the room has changed its sense of distance. The table is near and also impossibly far away. I can hear a woman asking for her son. A boy wants to know whether his bread is still warm. An old man is angry about a set of tools.
legacyText.3790640123: I say wait, and the voices wait. Not forever. Long enough for me to understand the difference.
legacyText.54729283: Julian disconnects the old receiving loop. Wren takes her card from the table. Her face steadies as the borrowed voices move towards me instead.
legacyText.823501949: Imani comes close enough that I can see the worn tape on the spare stick she brought from home.
legacyText.2775646901: “You don't get to turn into a job,” she says.
legacyText.1537366949: “No. Pick something ordinary. Something we can ask you about.”
legacyText.241429479: I look around the room. There is a chair near the switchboard, its seat split along one seam.
legacyText.2731216590: She nods, furious and crying now. “We'll start with that.”
legacyText.2337452029: Miso stays beside my chalk mark. Leila tells him to come. He looks at her and lies down.
legacyText.2116295455: He puts his head on his paws. “I'm not under claim.”
legacyText.2241720127: I cannot make him leave without contradicting the whole connection I just made.
legacyText.2062857742: Mum reaches me one last time. I am not sure whether she crossed the room or the room allowed her. She puts her uninjured hand against my cheek.
legacyText.1252418034: “I am going to be very difficult about this,” she says.
legacyText.765214862: Then Leila takes her towards the stairs. Julian carries the reader. Wren stops in the doorway and raises her hand. Imani follows last, looking back until the angle of the corridor takes me out of sight.
legacyText.2449276720: The station settles. It is smaller now. No borrowed corridors. No locked inner room. Just the table, the switchboard, the chair and a cat who has chosen to remain.
legacyText.3052624266: I sit down. The split seam catches my coat.
legacyText.861372197: At the first socket, a light comes on.
legacyText.896053023: I check the receiving conditions before lifting the handset.
legacyText.946975050: “Hello,” I say. “You can leave a message. You don't have to stay.”
legacyText.2099753443: I begin by trying to answer every light. Within an hour, I understand why Mum made lists.
legacyText.1214811509: Some people want a message carried. Some want to know why they were called. Some have been waiting so long they are angry before I speak. I tell each one what the line can do. I don't promise a receiver will answer.
legacyText.945341234: Miso finds a cupboard with a dry blanket inside and carries it to the foot of my chair. He spends a long time arranging it, then lies down on the bare floor beside it.
legacyText.239714708: “You could use that,” I tell him.
legacyText.1341057213: I pull it over my knees. The station is cold when nobody is moving through it.
legacyText.1231898385: At noon, the second reader opens a controlled line from the annex. Julian is on the other end. I can hear him testing the connection by reading out the time, then a list of objects on his desk.
legacyText.646012061: “Good. Don't answer when it's just the test tone.”
legacyText.2543727274: “I have learned one or two things.”
legacyText.2923473198: Mum comes on after him. She is in hospital. I can hear the soft bleep of a monitor and Leila talking to someone farther away.
legacyText.798770171: I look around the station. I'm not hungry. I don't know whether that is reassuring.
legacyText.1592809538: “I need to find out how that works here.”
legacyText.2078117153: For a while neither of us says anything else. I listen to the room around her. A trolley passes. Someone laughs. A plastic curtain slides along a rail. I would never have chosen a hospital as a place to miss so badly.
legacyText.3295857930: “{{firstName}},” she says at last. “I shouldn't have needed you to do this.”
legacyText.3456158184: She breathes out. I am glad I said it before it became one more thing neither of us could ask.
legacyText.3539699765: Wren comes on briefly. She tells me that snow melts at different speeds depending on what I put it on. She has been conducting tests on a windowsill, a glove and the sleeve of Julian's cardigan. He has objected to the cardigan.
legacyText.2458697576: “Good. Means we're talking to the right person.”
legacyText.609971959: I laugh for the first time since the stairs closed. Miso raises his head to check the sound, then puts it down again.
legacyText.905926654: After the call ends, I find a new line waiting on the board. It is not connected to a person. It has my number written beside it, in handwriting I recognise as my own.
legacyText.574010497: I examine the routing stamp. One day after arrival, not the day of departure. The date my phone showed. Nadia's manual calls it a reserved receiving slot.
legacyText.2427287231: I've spent two days wondering who was on the other end. Now the empty socket waits for a voice.
legacyText.1973317021: I check the return line against Mum's manual before using it. One message, back to the point where the first claim began. The date is a reserved receiving slot, a place in the route rather than a promise about which day the speaker belongs to.
legacyText.2801897773: It explains the wrong date on my phone. It does not make hearing my own breathing less strange.
legacyText.294802133: I give myself the notebook. The kitchen drawer. I start one last sentence and the line closes before I know how to finish it.
legacyText.620745773: Miso lifts his head from the blanket.
legacyText.1605366466: I turn to the next light.
legacyText.3727951660: The first week is hard in ways I didn't rehearse. I miss being able to leave a room because I am tired of it. I miss food I can complain about. I miss the sound the flat's radiator makes before it warms up.
legacyText.2840419852: I do not miss school until Julian brings my chemistry work through the controlled line. Then I miss the whole building, including the corridor where the lockers never close properly.
legacyText.2177023369: Mum calls every evening. Sometimes she talks about the receiving point she is trying to build. Sometimes she tells me what she bought at the supermarket. When she begins explaining an experiment without asking how I am, I interrupt her. The first time, she is hurt. The second time, she catches herself.
legacyText.1803350783: Leila keeps the calls from becoming only research. She asks about sleep, then listens when I say I don't know whether I am sleeping or merely resting between messages. She writes it down without pretending the answer is reassuring.
legacyText.780104074: Imani brings a chair. Getting it through the controlled route takes most of a Saturday and an argument with a door which appears not to recognise furniture as an authorised visitor. She refuses to leave it behind. When it finally arrives, the seat is scratched but intact.
legacyText.3181019891: I sit. It is an excellent chair.
legacyText.4125670492: She stands beside me for a while, looking at the board. A light comes on, then another. I let them wait. That is permitted now.
legacyText.688559573: I get up so quickly the chair scrapes backwards. She laughs, then I am hugging her, and for a minute the station contains a celebration which has nothing to do with being brave.
legacyText.4177980529: Wren visits with Julian. She is learning to write messages which belong only to her. Most are questions. Some are complaints about how many ordinary words have more than one meaning. She brings Miso a knitted mouse. He ignores it until she leaves, then carries it to the blanket.
legacyText.2402341854: Voss has not tried to call. The investigation continues above. Nadia has supplied the original manuals and signed a statement about her own work. Julian tells me the records will be complicated. I believe him. I have developed a strong dislike of stories which end when the person responsible looks sad enough.
legacyText.2954233958: I help a few callers each day. I turn down requests that would make somebody else answer by force. I ask the right question before accepting a message. Sometimes a receiver refuses. The refusal is recorded, and the line closes. No one is punished for it.
legacyText.2767072516: At the end of the third week, Mum reaches the station through the visitor route. Not a voice. A person. She has a bag of sandwiches and several pages of calculations held together by a bulldog clip.
legacyText.2506376992: She puts the calculations down first.
legacyText.2372819101: I look at her hand. It is healing. I look at the sandwiches, the ordinary grease showing through the paper.
legacyText.127497640: She sits in the old chair, which Imani repaired rather than throwing away.
legacyText.3409081201: So I do. Not everything. Enough to begin.
legacyText.1528949618: Later, she shows me the calculations. There may be a way to divide the station's role among several consenting operators, each with a defined shift and a way out. It is not ready. It is not a promise she can safely make. She tells me both facts before asking whether I want to help test it.
legacyText.1861405295: I read the first page. Make a correction in the margin. Ask a question.
legacyText.3050758331: Mum smiles at the familiar impatience in my voice.
legacyText.1731860499: On the switchboard, a light comes on. I check its conditions, then lift the receiver.
legacyText.3763439665: Miso closes his eyes in the warm patch beside my new chair. Mum opens her notebook. Somewhere above me, people are having an ordinary evening, and the controlled line home remains open.
legacyText.563777855: At least, it was when I locked the door.

hearts.title: Return hearts
hearts.description: Chances to survive a broken supernatural connection. Ordinary injuries do not spend them.

seal.title: Scribe Seal
levels: Sense where a drawn seal leaks. Hold one small, named connection for a few breaths.
Correct a moving inscription while someone else holds its source.
Share a seal across two prepared surfaces. Neither can hold a person indefinitely.
seal.cost: Numb fingers and lost concentration. A seal cannot command a living person.

sight.title: Spirit Sight
levels: Sense a nearby spirit through one existing connection.
Distinguish a remembered voice from a present speaker; ask one clear question.
Anchor a consenting spirit briefly to a prepared receiving point.
sight.cost: Listening carries both ways. A spirit may notice the listener; hearing does not establish consent.

sunward.title: Sunward
levels: Borrow existing light to show an obscured mark.
Turn that light into a brief screen against a false reflection.
Hold the screen while another person crosses. It still needs a light source.
sunward.cost: After-images and a severe headache. It neither revives the dead nor burns through a god.

fracture.title: Broken Reflection
levels: Split a false signal into two imperfect decoys.
Choose which decoy carries the louder return.
Interrupt a claim for a few seconds while another person releases it.
fracture.cost: Every use leaves a recognisable echo. Forcing an occupied line can consume a return heart.

sheetSections.title: The sealed record
sheetSections.text: Thoth is my divine father. Mum and he concealed his signature behind a witness seal to hide my return from the Exchange. Leila trusted the covered copy. His absence was a decision, not proof he could not help.

protagonist.name: {{fullName}}
protagonist.text: I live in Toronto. Before Friday, the biggest unfinished thing in my life was Mum’s disappearance.

Imani.name: Imani
Imani.text: Goalie. Third floor. Her own Saturday matters.

Wren.name: Wren
Wren.text: She chose her name. She is not Eva.
